title: How to Run Orchestration Tests
content:
# How to Run Orchestration Tests

Guide for running the orchestration E2E test suite, which validates the full orchestration lifecycle: task creation, daemon dispatch, worker execution, and steward review.

## Overview

The test suite has two modes:
- **Mock mode** (default): Uses a mock session manager. Fast, no external dependencies.
- **Real mode**: Spawns actual `claude` processes via `SpawnerService`. Requires `claude` in PATH.

All 12 tests support both modes. Mock mode simulates agent behavior; real mode lets Claude actually execute tasks.

## Quick Start

> **Note:** The `test:orchestration` script is defined in `packages/smithy/package.json`. Run these commands from the `packages/smithy/` directory.

### Run all tests (mock mode)

```bash
cd packages/smithy
bun run test:orchestration
```

### Run all tests (real mode)

```bash
cd packages/smithy
bun run test:orchestration --mode real --verbose
```

## CLI Flags

| Flag | Short | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `--mode <mock\|real>` | `-m` | Test mode (default: `mock`) |
| `--test <id>` | `-t` | Run specific test by ID (substring match) |
| `--tag <tag>` | | Filter tests by tag (`director`, `worker`, `steward`, `daemon`) |
| `--bail` | | Stop on first failure |
| `--verbose` | `-v` | Enable verbose logging |
| `--timeout <ms>` | | Override timeout for each test |
| `--skip-cleanup` | | Preserve temp workspace after run (for debugging) |
| `--help` | `-h` | Show help |

## Examples

### Run a single test

```bash
bun run test:orchestration --test "worker-marks-task-complete"
```

### Run tests by category

```bash
bun run test:orchestration --tag worker
bun run test:orchestration --tag director
bun run test:orchestration --tag steward
bun run test:orchestration --tag daemon
```

### Run real mode with bail and debugging

```bash
bun run test:orchestration --mode real --tag worker --bail --verbose --skip-cleanup
```

When `--skip-cleanup` is used, the temp workspace path is printed so you can inspect the git repo, worktrees, and database.

## Test List

| # | ID | Tags | What it validates |
|---|-----|------|-------------------|
| 1 | `director-creates-tasks` | director, task | Director creates a task from a prompt |
| 2 | `director-creates-plans` | director, plan | Director creates a multi-task plan |
| 3 | `daemon-dispatches-worker` | daemon, dispatch, worker | Daemon assigns unassigned task to available worker |
| 4 | `daemon-respects-dependencies` | daemon, dependencies | Blocked task waits until dependency resolves |
| 5 | `worker-uses-worktree` | worker, worktree, git | Worker operates in an isolated git worktree |
| 6 | `worker-commits-work` | worker, git, commit | Worker commits changes to its worktree branch |
| 7 | `worker-creates-merge-request` | worker, merge-request, git | Worker sets branch/MR metadata on task completion |
| 8 | `worker-marks-task-complete` | worker, task, completion | Task status transitions to closed |
| 9 | `worker-handoff-context` | worker, handoff, context | Worker creates handoff before context exhaustion |
| 10 | `daemon-spawns-steward-mr` | daemon, steward, merge-request | Merge request event triggers steward spawn |
| 11 | `steward-merges-passing` | steward, merge, tests | Steward merges PR when tests pass |
| 12 | `steward-handoff-failing` | steward, handoff, tests | Steward hands off to worker when tests fail |

## Timeouts

Mock mode uses per-test timeouts (30s-120s). Real mode applies longer category-based defaults:

| Category | Real mode timeout |
|----------|------------------|
| Director tests (1-2) | 240s |
| Daemon tests (3-4) | 180s |
| Worker tests (5-9) | 300s |
| Steward tests (10-12) | 300s |

Use `--timeout <ms>` to override.

## Test Environment

Each test run creates an isolated temporary workspace with:
- Fresh git repository with initial commit
- Local bare remote (`.test-remote.git`) for push operations
- Minimal project structure (`package.json`, `src/index.ts`, `README.md`)
- SQLite database in `.stoneforge/stoneforge.db`
- All orchestration services (daemon, agent registry, worktree manager, etc.)

In real mode, constrained prompt overrides are written to `.stoneforge/prompts/` to guide agents toward fast, deterministic behavior.

## Key Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `packages/smithy/src/testing/test-context.ts` | Test workspace setup, mode toggle, cleanup |
| `packages/smithy/src/testing/orchestration-tests.ts` | All 12 test definitions (mock + real paths) |
| `packages/smithy/src/testing/test-utils.ts` | Polling helpers and assertions |
| `packages/smithy/src/testing/test-prompts.ts` | Constrained prompts for real-mode agents |
| `packages/smithy/src/cli/commands/test-orchestration.ts` | CLI runner and flag parsing |
| `packages/smithy/src/testing/index.ts` | Public exports |

## Troubleshooting

**Tests pass in mock but fail in real mode**: Real mode depends on `claude` being installed and accessible. Verify with `which claude`.

**Orphan processes after interrupted run**: The cleanup handler registers SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers, but if the process is killed with SIGKILL, orphan `claude` processes may remain. Check with `ps aux | grep claude` and kill manually.

**Debugging a failing test**: Use `--skip-cleanup` to preserve the workspace, then inspect the git log, worktrees, and database in the temp directory.

# AgentRegistry Reference

**File:** `packages/smithy/src/services/agent-registry.ts` (from `@stoneforge/smithy`)

The `AgentRegistry` manages agent registration, querying, session management, and dedicated channel operations within the orchestration system. Agents are stored as `Entity` elements with role-specific metadata under the `'agent'` key.

**Key type:** `AgentEntity` — an `Entity` with agent metadata. Use the `getAgentMetadata(entity)` helper to extract typed `AgentMetadata` from an `AgentEntity`.

---

## Agent Registration

### registerAgent()

```typescript
registerAgent(input: RegisterAgentInput): Promise<AgentEntity>
```

Registers a new agent by dispatching to the appropriate role-specific method based on `input.role`.

**Parameters:**
- `input` — A discriminated union of registration inputs:
  - `RegisterDirectorInput & { role: 'director' }`
  - `RegisterWorkerInput & { role: 'worker' }`
  - `RegisterStewardInput & { role: 'steward' }`

**Returns:** The newly created `AgentEntity`.

---

### registerDirector()

```typescript
registerDirector(input: RegisterDirectorInput): Promise<AgentEntity>
```

Registers a Director agent. There should typically be only one Director per workspace.

**Parameters (`RegisterDirectorInput`):**
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Unique agent name |
| `createdBy` | `EntityId` | Yes | Entity ID of the creator (usually a human) |
| `tags` | `string[]` | No | Optional tags for the agent entity |
| `maxConcurrentTasks` | `number` | No | Max concurrent tasks (default: 1) |
| `roleDefinitionRef` | `ElementId` | No | Reference to a role definition Document for system prompt/behaviors |
| `provider` | `string` | No | Agent provider (e.g., `'claude-code'`, `'opencode'`). Defaults to `'claude-code'` |
| `model` | `string` | No | Model identifier (e.g., `'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'`). Uses provider default if unset |
| `executablePath` | `string` | No | Custom executable path for the provider CLI |
| `targetBranch` | `string` | No | Target branch for merges (e.g., `'staging'`). Defaults to repository default branch |

**Returns:** The newly created `AgentEntity`.

---

### registerWorker()

```typescript
registerWorker(input: RegisterWorkerInput): Promise<AgentEntity>
```

Registers a Worker agent. Workers can be ephemeral (short-lived, task-specific) or persistent (long-lived, multi-task).

**Parameters (`RegisterWorkerInput`):**
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Unique agent name |
| `workerMode` | `WorkerMode` | Yes | `'ephemeral'` or `'persistent'` |
| `createdBy` | `EntityId` | Yes | Entity ID of the creator |
| `reportsTo` | `EntityId` | No | Manager entity (Director for ephemeral, Human for persistent) |
| `tags` | `string[]` | No | Optional tags for the agent entity |
| `maxConcurrentTasks` | `number` | No | Max concurrent tasks (default: 1) |
| `roleDefinitionRef` | `ElementId` | No | Reference to a role definition Document |
| `provider` | `string` | No | Agent provider. Defaults to `'claude-code'` |
| `model` | `string` | No | Model identifier. Uses provider default if unset |
| `executablePath` | `string` | No | Custom executable path for the provider CLI |

**Returns:** The newly created `AgentEntity`.

---

### registerSteward()

```typescript
registerSteward(input: RegisterStewardInput): Promise<AgentEntity>
```

Registers a Steward agent. Stewards perform support tasks like merging branches, scanning documentation, or executing custom playbooks.

**Parameters (`RegisterStewardInput`):**
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Unique agent name |
| `stewardFocus` | `StewardFocus` | Yes | `'merge'`, `'docs'`, `'recovery'`, or `'custom'` |
| `createdBy` | `EntityId` | Yes | Entity ID of the creator |
| `triggers` | `StewardTrigger[]` | No | Triggers that activate this steward (cron or event-based) |
| `playbook` | `string` | No | _(Deprecated)_ Inline playbook content for custom stewards. Prefer `playbookId` |
| `playbookId` | `string` | No | Reference to a Workflow Template for custom stewards |
| `reportsTo` | `EntityId` | No | Manager entity (usually the Director) |
| `tags` | `string[]` | No | Optional tags for the agent entity |
| `maxConcurrentTasks` | `number` | No | Max concurrent tasks (default: 1) |
| `roleDefinitionRef` | `ElementId` | No | Reference to a role definition Document |
| `provider` | `string` | No | Agent provider. Defaults to `'claude-code'` |
| `model` | `string` | No | Model identifier. Uses provider default if unset |
| `executablePath` | `string` | No | Custom executable path for the provider CLI |

**Returns:** The newly created `AgentEntity`.

---

## Agent Queries

### getAgent()

```typescript
getAgent(entityId: EntityId): Promise<AgentEntity | undefined>
```

Gets an agent by its entity ID.

**Parameters:**
- `entityId` — The unique entity ID of the agent.

**Returns:** The `AgentEntity` if found, or `undefined`.

---

### getAgentByName()

```typescript
getAgentByName(name: string): Promise<AgentEntity | undefined>
```

Gets an agent by its name.

**Parameters:**
- `name` — The agent's name (names are unique across the workspace).

**Returns:** The `AgentEntity` if found, or `undefined`.

---

### listAgents()

```typescript
listAgents(filter?: AgentFilter): Promise<AgentEntity[]>
```

Lists agents matching the given filter criteria. Returns all agents if no filter is provided.

**Parameters:**
- `filter` _(optional)_ — An `AgentFilter` object:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `role` | `AgentRole` | Filter by role (`'director'`, `'steward'`, `'worker'`) |
| `workerMode` | `WorkerMode` | Filter by worker mode (only when `role` is `'worker'`) |
| `stewardFocus` | `StewardFocus` | Filter by steward focus (only when `role` is `'steward'`) |
| `sessionStatus` | `'idle' \| 'running' \| 'suspended' \| 'terminated'` | Filter by session status |
| `reportsTo` | `EntityId` | Filter by manager entity |
| `hasSession` | `boolean` | Include only agents with active sessions |

**Returns:** Array of matching `AgentEntity` objects.

**Example:**
```typescript
// Get all running workers
const workers = await registry.listAgents({
  role: 'worker',
  sessionStatus: 'running',
});

// Get all ephemeral workers
const ephemeral = await registry.listAgents({
  role: 'worker',
  workerMode: 'ephemeral',
});
```

---

### getAgentsByRole()

```typescript
getAgentsByRole(role: AgentRole): Promise<AgentEntity[]>
```

Gets all agents with a specific role. Convenience wrapper around `listAgents({ role })`.

**Parameters:**
- `role` — `'director'`, `'steward'`, or `'worker'`.

**Returns:** Array of `AgentEntity` objects with the given role.

---

### getAvailableWorkers()

```typescript
getAvailableWorkers(): Promise<AgentEntity[]>
```

Gets workers that are idle or have capacity for more tasks.

**Returns:** Array of `AgentEntity` objects representing available workers.

---

### getStewards()

```typescript
getStewards(): Promise<AgentEntity[]>
```

Gets all steward agents. Convenience wrapper around `listAgents({ role: 'steward' })`.

**Returns:** Array of steward `AgentEntity` objects.

---

### getDirector()

```typescript
getDirector(): Promise<AgentEntity | undefined>
```

Returns the first registered director agent. Internally calls `listAgents({ role: 'director' })` and returns the first result.

For multi-director workspaces, use `getDirectors()` instead.

**Returns:** The first `AgentEntity` with role `'director'`, or `undefined` if none registered.

---

### getDirectors()

```typescript
getDirectors(): Promise<AgentEntity[]>
```

Gets all Director agents registered in the workspace.

**Returns:** Array of director `AgentEntity` objects.

---

### getAvailableDirector()

```typescript
getAvailableDirector(preferredId?: EntityId): Promise<AgentEntity | undefined>
```

Gets an available (running) director, with optional preference.

**Parameters:**
- `preferredId` _(optional)_ — Preferred director entity ID. If this director is running, it is returned.

**Returns:** The preferred director if running, otherwise any running director, or `undefined` if no directors are running.

---

## Agent Session Management

### updateAgentSession()

```typescript
updateAgentSession(
  entityId: EntityId,
  sessionId: string | undefined,
  status: 'idle' | 'running' | 'suspended' | 'terminated'
): Promise<AgentEntity>
```

Updates an agent's session status and provider session ID.

**Parameters:**
- `entityId` — The agent's entity ID.
- `sessionId` — The provider session ID for resumption, or `undefined` to clear.
- `status` — The new session status: `'idle'`, `'running'`, `'suspended'`, or `'terminated'`.

**Returns:** The updated `AgentEntity`.

---

### updateAgentMetadata()

```typescript
updateAgentMetadata(
  entityId: EntityId,
  updates: Partial<AgentMetadata>
): Promise<AgentEntity>
```

Updates an agent's metadata with a partial update. Only the fields provided in `updates` are changed; other metadata fields are preserved.

**Parameters:**
- `entityId` — The agent's entity ID.
- `updates` — Partial `AgentMetadata` fields to merge (e.g., `{ sessionStatus: 'idle', lastActivityAt: timestamp }`).

**Returns:** The updated `AgentEntity`.

---

### updateAgent()

```typescript
updateAgent(
  entityId: EntityId,
  updates: { name?: string }
): Promise<AgentEntity>
```

Updates an agent's top-level properties (currently only the agent name).

**Parameters:**
- `entityId` — The agent's entity ID.
- `updates` — Object with optional `name` field.

**Returns:** The updated `AgentEntity`.

---

### deleteAgent()

```typescript
deleteAgent(entityId: EntityId): Promise<void>
```

Deletes an agent and its associated dedicated channel.

**Parameters:**
- `entityId` — The agent's entity ID.

**Returns:** `void`.

---

## Agent Channel Operations

Each agent has a dedicated direct channel for receiving messages. Channels are created using `createDirectChannel` with names in the format `{sortedEntityId}:{sortedEntityId}` (e.g., `el-0000:el-abcd`). These methods manage those channels.

### getAgentChannel()

```typescript
getAgentChannel(agentId: EntityId): Promise<Channel | undefined>
```

Gets the dedicated channel for an agent.

**Parameters:**
- `agentId` — The entity ID of the agent.

**Returns:** The agent's `Channel`, or `undefined` if not found.

---

### getAgentChannelId()

```typescript
getAgentChannelId(agentId: EntityId): Promise<ChannelId | undefined>
```

Gets the channel ID for an agent from its metadata. This is faster than `getAgentChannel()` when you only need the ID, as it reads from metadata without fetching the full channel object.

**Parameters:**
- `agentId` — The entity ID of the agent.

**Returns:** The `ChannelId`, or `undefined` if the agent has no channel.

---

### ensureAgentChannel()

```typescript
ensureAgentChannel(agentId: EntityId): Promise<Channel>
```

Ensures an agent has a dedicated channel. If the channel is missing (e.g., due to a partial registration failure, JSONL sync issue, or crash), it is recreated and the agent's metadata is updated with the new channel ID. Logs a warning when a channel needs to be recreated.

**Parameters:**
- `agentId` — The entity ID of the agent.

**Returns:** The agent's `Channel` (existing or newly created).

---

## Factory Function

### createAgentRegistry()

```typescript
function createAgentRegistry(api: QuarryAPI): AgentRegistry
```

Creates a new `AgentRegistry` instance. This is the canonical way to instantiate the registry.

**Parameters:**
- `api` — A `QuarryAPI` instance for underlying element operations.

**Returns:** An `AgentRegistry` implementation.

**Example:**
```typescript
import { createAgentRegistry } from '@stoneforge/smithy';

const registry = createAgentRegistry(api);
const workers = await registry.listAgents({ role: 'worker' });
```

---

## Exported Utilities

The module also exports several utility functions:

### generateAgentChannelName()

```typescript
function generateAgentChannelName(agentName: string): string
```

Generates the channel name for an agent. Returns `agent-{agentName}`.

### parseAgentChannelName()

```typescript
function parseAgentChannelName(channelName: string): string | null
```

Parses an agent name from a channel name. Returns `null` if the name doesn't match the `agent-` prefix pattern.

### Re-exports

- `AgentEntity` (type) — Agent entity type
- `isAgentEntity` — Type guard for `AgentEntity`
- `getAgentMetadata` — Extracts typed `AgentMetadata` from an `AgentEntity`

---

## Related Types

For full type definitions, see `packages/smithy/src/types/agent.ts`:

- **`AgentRole`** — `'director' | 'steward' | 'worker'`
- **`WorkerMode`** — `'ephemeral' | 'persistent'`
- **`StewardFocus`** — `'merge' | 'docs' | 'recovery' | 'custom'`
- **`StewardTrigger`** — `CronTrigger | EventTrigger`
- **`AgentMetadata`** — `DirectorMetadata | WorkerMetadata | StewardMetadata`
- **`AgentFilter`** — Filter options for `listAgents()`

title: Storage Reference
content:
# Storage Reference

**Package:** `@stoneforge/storage` (`packages/storage/src/`)

SQLite storage layer with multiple backend implementations.

## Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SQLite                        │
│  Fast queries, indexes, full-text search        │
│            (cache, ephemeral)                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                      ↕ sync
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    JSONL                         │
│   Git-tracked, append-only, mergeable           │
│           (source of truth)                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Key Principle:** SQLite is the **cache**, JSONL is the **source of truth**.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `index.ts` | Type exports |
| `backend.ts` | StorageBackend interface |
| `create-backend.ts` | Factory: `createStorage()`, `createStorageAsync()` |
| `bun-backend.ts` | Bun native implementation |
| `node-backend.ts` | Node.js (better-sqlite3) implementation |
| `browser-backend.ts` | Browser (WASM + OPFS) implementation |
| `schema.ts` | SQLite schema and migrations |
| `dirty.ts` | Shared dirty-tracking SQL (atomic mark statement, floor triggers) |
| `types.ts` | Transaction, QueryResult, PreparedStatement |
| `errors.ts` | `mapStorageError()`, constraint detection |

## Creating Storage

```typescript
import { createStorage, initializeSchema } from '@stoneforge/storage';

// Auto-detects runtime (Bun, Node, Browser)
const storage = createStorage({ path: './project/.stoneforge/stoneforge.db' });

// Initialize schema
initializeSchema(storage);

// Async variant (for browser WASM)
const storage = await createStorageAsync({ path: './stoneforge.db' });
```

## StorageBackend Interface

**All methods are synchronous** (not async/Promise).

```typescript
interface StorageBackend {
  // Connection
  readonly isOpen: boolean;
  readonly path: string;
  readonly inTransaction: boolean;
  close(): void;

  // SQL Execution
  exec(sql: string): void;
  query<T>(sql: string, params?: unknown[]): T[];
  queryOne<T>(sql: string, params?: unknown[]): T | undefined;
  run(sql: string, params?: unknown[]): MutationResult;
  prepare<T>(sql: string): PreparedStatement<T>;

  // Transactions
  transaction<T>(fn: (tx: Transaction) => T, options?: TransactionOptions): T;

  // Schema
  getSchemaVersion(): number;
  setSchemaVersion(version: number): void;
  migrate(migrations: Migration[]): MigrationResult;

  // Dirty Tracking
  markDirty(elementId: string): void;
  getDirtyElements(options?: DirtyTrackingOptions): DirtyElement[];
  clearDirty(): void;
  clearDirtyElements(elementIds: string[]): void;
  clearDirtySnapshot(snapshot: DirtyElement[]): number;

  // Hierarchical IDs
  getNextChildNumber(parentId: string): number;
  getChildCounter(parentId: string): number;
  resetChildCounter(parentId: string): void;
  getElementCount(): number;

  // Utilities
  checkIntegrity(): boolean;
  optimize(): void;  // VACUUM + ANALYZE
  getStats(): StorageStats;
}
```

## Dirty Tracking

Elements modified since last export are marked "dirty":

```typescript
storage.markDirty(elementId);
const dirty = storage.getDirtyElements();
// Returns: { elementId: string, markedAt: string }[]

storage.clearDirtySnapshot(snapshot);     // Clear only marks captured in a
                                          // snapshot that were not re-marked
storage.clearDirtyElements(elementIds);   // Clear specific (unsafe after a read)
storage.clearDirty();                     // Clear all (unsafe after a read)
```

**Note:** `getDirtyElements()` returns `DirtyElement` records, not full Element objects.

### The dirty-tracking guarantee

Dirty marks acknowledge JSONL exports, so the clear must never acknowledge a
change that was **not** exported. The `marked_at` column acts as a per-element
change **token**, and the following invariants make a safe clear possible:

1. **`markDirty()` is a single atomic statement.** It is one `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` (UPSERT) whose new token is computed *inside* SQLite from the currently stored row and the global token floor (the shared SQL lives in `packages/storage/src/dirty.ts`; all three backends execute it). SQLite serializes write statements across connections, so two connections can never read the same old token and issue the same new one — the historical SELECT-then-`INSERT OR REPLACE` implementation allowed exactly that race, and an export snapshot holding the duplicated token would then erase the other writer's mark. Being a single statement also means it is safe inside an already-open transaction.
2. **Tokens are strictly monotonic per element.** A re-mark always records a strictly greater `marked_at` than the element's current mark — when the wall clock has not advanced (two marks in the same millisecond) the stored value is bumped by 1ms. A mark is therefore always distinguishable from any mark captured before it.
3. **Tokens are never reused — even after the row is cleared.** Every issued token advances a global high-water mark (`dirty_token_floor`, one row, maintained by triggers that execute atomically within the marking statement). A fresh — or re-created-after-clear — row takes `max(wall clock, floor + 1ms)`. Without this, overlapping exports at the same millisecond could regenerate the exact token an older, still-in-flight export snapshot holds, and that export's `clearDirtySnapshot()` would erase the newer change.

Unparseable legacy `marked_at` values are overwritten with a fresh token and never poison the floor. The `dirty_elements`, `dirty_token_floor` tables and their triggers are created idempotently on every connection open (they live outside the versioned migration set), so existing databases upgrade automatically.

4. **`clearDirtySnapshot(snapshot)` clears conditionally.** Each snapshot entry (an `{ elementId, markedAt }` pair captured with `getDirtyElements()` before the export's writes began) clears its dirty row only if the row still carries exactly that `marked_at`. A row re-marked since the snapshot has a strictly newer `marked_at` and stays dirty, so the newer change is exported next time. Entries whose row no longer exists are skipped (and, by invariant 3, cannot have been re-created with the snapshotted token). The deletes are batched in a transaction (unless one is already open) and the return value is the number of rows actually cleared.

`SyncService` relies on all of this: `prepareExport()` snapshots the dirty set **before** reading any element data, and after the (async) file writes succeed the export clears only that snapshot. Anything mutated while the writes were awaited keeps its dirty mark and goes out in the next incremental export.

`clearDirty()` and `clearDirtyElements()` remain for non-export uses (tests, resets), but on any path where the clear happens after an `await` or after other storage reads they can silently drop pending changes — prefer `clearDirtySnapshot()` with a fresh `getDirtyElements()` snapshot. (They cannot, however, cause token reuse: the floor survives every form of clear.)

## Transactions

```typescript
const result = storage.transaction((tx) => {
  tx.run('INSERT INTO elements ...');
  tx.run('INSERT INTO dependencies ...');
  return 'success';
}, {
  isolation: 'immediate',  // 'deferred' | 'immediate' | 'exclusive'
});
```

## Database Location

Default: `.stoneforge/` directory in project root

```
.stoneforge/
├── stoneforge.db   # SQLite database
├── sync/
│   ├── elements.jsonl      # JSONL export (source of truth)
│   └── dependencies.jsonl  # Dependency relationships
└── config.yaml     # Project configuration
```

## Schema

Current version: 13

### Key Tables

| Table | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `elements` | All elements with JSON data column |
| `dependencies` | Relationship records |
| `dirty_elements` | Dirty tracking (auto-created in constructor) |
| `dirty_token_floor` | High-water mark of issued dirty tokens; makes token reuse impossible after clears (auto-created in constructor) |
| `blocked_cache` | Materialized blocked status |
| `child_counters` | Hierarchical ID counters |
| `document_versions` | Version history for documents |
| `tags` | Tag index for fast filtering |
| `events` | System events for audit/history |
| `inbox_items` | Notification items per entity |
| `comments` | Inline document comments with text anchoring (migration 5) |
| `session_messages` | Persistent session event storage for agent sessions (migration 6) |
| `documents_fts` | FTS5 virtual table for full-text document search (migration 7) |
| `document_embeddings` | Vector embeddings for semantic document search (migration 8) |
| `settings` | Server-side key-value configuration store (migration 9) |
| `operation_log` | Structured operation logs for dispatch, merge, session, rate-limit, steward, recovery events (migration 10) |
| `provider_metrics` | Per-request LLM provider metrics including token counts, latency, cache usage, and outcome (migration 10, extended in migration 12) |

### Elements Table

```sql
CREATE TABLE elements (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  data TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON blob
  content_hash TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at TEXT,
  CHECK (type IN ('task', 'message', 'document', 'entity',
                  'plan', 'workflow', 'playbook',
                  'channel', 'library', 'team'))
);
```

### Dependencies Table

```sql
CREATE TABLE dependencies (
  blocked_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES elements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  blocker_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  type TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
  metadata TEXT,  -- JSON blob
  PRIMARY KEY (blocked_id, blocker_id, type)
);
```

**Note:** Only `blocked_id` has a CASCADE foreign key constraint. Deleting the blocked element removes its dependencies.

### FTS5 Virtual Table (Migration 7)

```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE documents_fts USING fts5(
  document_id UNINDEXED,
  title,
  content,
  tags,
  category UNINDEXED,
  tokenize='porter unicode61'
);
```

External-content FTS5 index for documents. Uses BM25 ranking and supports snippet generation. Populated by `QuarryAPI` on document create/update/delete (not via triggers). The `document_id` and `category` columns are `UNINDEXED` (stored but not searchable).

### Document Embeddings Table (Migration 8)

```sql
CREATE TABLE document_embeddings (
  document_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  embedding BLOB NOT NULL,
  dimensions INTEGER NOT NULL,
  provider TEXT NOT NULL,
  model TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (document_id) REFERENCES elements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

Stores vector embeddings for semantic search. Embeddings are generated by a registered `EmbeddingProvider` and used for cosine-similarity document retrieval.

### Migration 11: Update inbox_items CHECK constraint

Adds `thread_reply` to the `inbox_items.source_type` CHECK constraint. The original migration 4 only allowed `('direct', 'mention')`, but the core type system defines `InboxSourceType.THREAD_REPLY = 'thread_reply'`. Since SQLite does not support `ALTER CONSTRAINT`, the table is recreated with the updated constraint: `CHECK (source_type IN ('direct', 'mention', 'thread_reply'))`.

### Migration 12: Add cache token columns to provider_metrics

Adds `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_creation_tokens` columns (both `INTEGER DEFAULT 0`) to the `provider_metrics` table for tracking Anthropic API prompt cache usage alongside regular input/output tokens.

### Migration 13: Ordering indexes on elements

```sql
-- (type, ...) serves single-type filters; (deleted_at, ...) serves the
-- no-type and multi-type paths, where `deleted_at IS NULL` is the leading
-- equality term; (updated_at) serves the unfiltered includeDeleted path,
-- which has no leading equality term (created_at got one in migration 1).
-- One index per column pair: the rowid tiebreaker mirrors the query
-- direction, so forward and backward scans of the same index serve
-- asc and desc pages without a temp b-tree sort.
CREATE INDEX idx_elements_type_created_at            ON elements(type, created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_elements_type_updated_at            ON elements(type, updated_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_elements_deleted_at_created_at      ON elements(deleted_at, created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_elements_deleted_at_updated_at      ON elements(deleted_at, updated_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_elements_updated_at                 ON elements(updated_at);
```

These exist so `QuarryAPI.list()/listPaginated()` can serve `WHERE type = ? [AND deleted_at IS NULL] ORDER BY <created_at|updated_at> <ASC|DESC> LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` by reading rows straight out of the index in LIMIT-first order. Before them, SQLite satisfied the type constraint with `idx_elements_type` and built temp b-trees for `DISTINCT` and `ORDER BY` over the **entire** match set, so even a fixed 50-row page cost O(n) in table size.

Notes:

- **One index per column pair serves both directions.** A B-tree stores equal keys in ascending rowid order, so a forward scan of `(leading, col)` yields `col ASC, rowid ASC` and a backward scan yields `col DESC, rowid DESC`. Because callers end every ordering with a tiebreaker that mirrors the query direction — `ORDER BY <col> <dir>, e.rowid <dir>`; `list()`/`listPaginated()` (via `buildListQuery`), `search()`, `searchChannels()` and sync `getAllElements()` — either scan satisfies the ORDER BY as written, and no direction-paired `_asc`/`_desc` duplicates are needed. (A mixed `<col> DESC, rowid ASC` matches no single-direction scan and would force a sort.)
- **Tie order is deterministic and it changed.** Tied rows come back in ascending rowid order for `asc` and descending rowid order for `desc`. The old tie order was never defined behavior — it depended on whichever plan SQLite picked (a stable sort fed by a rowid-ordered scan on type-filtered paths, a reversed index scan on unfiltered `includeDeleted` paths) — and reproducing it is explicitly not part of the contract; see the decision log (`sf show el-2mnn98`) for the Director's clarification of the criterion.
- `(deleted_at, ...)` covers the no-type and multi-type (`type IN (...)`) paths, because `deleted_at IS NULL` is on every default query and becomes the leading equality term.
- **Cost:** five new indexes on the hottest write table. The `created_at`-keyed ones change only on insert/delete and soft-delete transitions; the `updated_at`-keyed ones change on every element update. Accepted because element writes are far less frequent than list reads; see the decision log (`sf show el-2mnn98`).
- `idx_elements_type`, `idx_elements_created_at` and `idx_elements_deleted_at` are now largely redundant with the composites but are kept for compatibility. They are candidates for removal in a future migration.
- Orderings on JSON fields (`orderBy: 'title'`, `'status'`, ...) still materialize a temp b-tree — `JSON_EXTRACT` cannot use an index. Filtering on a `created_at` range while ordering by `updated_at` also keeps a temp b-tree (the index serves the range, not the ordering). See the decision log (`sf show el-2mnn98`) for the trade-offs.
- The plan, the old-vs-new result equivalence and the tie ordering are pinned by `packages/quarry/src/api/list-query-plan.bun.test.ts`, which runs the pre-change query against the pre-change index set (migrations 1–12): with distinct sort keys the results must match exactly (both directions, every pagination boundary, including the unfiltered `includeDeleted` and timestamp-range paths); with ties, the row sets and sort-key sequences must match and the explicit tiebreaker plus page-walk stability are asserted.

---

## Sync System

**Files:** `packages/quarry/src/sync/`

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `service.ts` | SyncService: export/import operations |
| `serialization.ts` | Element serialization/deserialization |
| `merge.ts` | Merge resolution logic (import side) |
| `incremental.ts` | Incremental export line merging (export side) |
| `auto-export.ts` | AutoExportService: polls dirty elements and exports |
| `hash.ts` | Content hash computation |
| `types.ts` | Sync-related types |

### JSONL Format

```jsonl
{"id":"abc123","type":"task","title":"...","createdAt":"...","createdBy":"..."}
{"id":"def456","type":"entity","name":"...","createdAt":"...","createdBy":"..."}
{"id":"abc123","type":"task","title":"...","status":"tombstone","deletedAt":"2026-10-03T12:00:00.000Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-03T12:00:00.000Z","createdBy":"..."}
```

Each line is a complete, self-contained JSON object. A soft-deleted element is
exported as a **tombstone** — the normal serialized element with
`status: "tombstone"` and `deletedAt` set (mirroring how `deleteElement()`
stores the tombstone in the element's `data` payload and the `deleted_at`
column).

### Export

```typescript
import { createSyncService } from '@stoneforge/quarry';

const syncService = createSyncService(storage);

// Incremental — merges dirty elements into the existing elements.jsonl
await syncService.export({ outputDir: '.stoneforge/sync' });

// Full export — rewrites the file from the complete element set
await syncService.export({ outputDir: '.stoneforge/sync', full: true });
```

**Both full and incremental exports include soft-deleted elements as
tombstones.** Deletions are part of the source of truth: a full export that
omitted soft-deleted rows (`deleted_at IS NULL` filtering) would erase
tombstones that earlier incremental exports had recorded, and any clone
importing the file would resurrect the deleted elements (this was a real bug,
fixed 2026-10 — see Critical Gotchas). `exportToString()` — which backs
`QuarryAPI.export()` and the HTTP sync pull/push/exchange endpoints — includes
tombstones for the same reason: replicas must learn about deletions. On
import, `deletedAt`/`deleted_at` are restored and a fresh tombstone wins over
a live element (see Merge Strategy below), so export → import round-trips
deletions. Ephemeral filtering is unaffected: tombstones of ephemeral
workflows are excluded exactly like their live counterparts.

**An incremental export never shrinks `elements.jsonl`.** Only elements marked
dirty are re-serialized; they replace their own line (keyed by `id`) or are
appended, and every other line is copied through byte-for-byte — including
tombstone lines for elements deleted earlier. The result is
re-sorted into the standard export order and written atomically (temp file +
rename), so a crash mid-write cannot truncate the source of truth. If
`elements.jsonl` is missing or unreadable, the incremental export falls back to
a full export (reported as `fallbackToFull: true` on the result).

Because the JSONL files are the git-tracked source of truth, an incremental
export that *replaced* the file with only the dirty subset would destroy data —
this was a real bug (fixed 2026-10, see Critical Gotchas). Note that
`ExportResult.elementsExported` is the number of lines in the written file (the
merged total), not the number of dirty elements.

Both JSONL files keep the historical terminal-newline convention: nonempty
content ends with exactly one `\n`, and an export with nothing to write produces
an empty file. `wc -l` therefore reports the element count exactly, and
re-exports diff cleanly against files written by earlier versions.

### Import

```typescript
// Standard import (merge)
const result = await syncService.import({ inputDir: '.stoneforge/sync' });
// result.elementsImported, result.elementsSkipped, result.conflicts

// Force import (remote always wins)
await syncService.import({ inputDir: '.stoneforge/sync', force: true });
```

### Serialization

```typescript
import {
  serializeElement,
  parseElement,
  serializeDependency,
  parseDependency,
} from '@stoneforge/quarry';

// Element → JSON string
const json = serializeElement(element);

// JSON string → Element
const element = parseElement(json);
```

### SerializedElement

```typescript
interface SerializedElement {
  id: string;
  type: ElementType;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  createdBy: string;
  tags: string[];
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
  // ... type-specific fields
}
```

### Content Hashing

Content hash is computed for merge conflict detection:

```typescript
import { computeContentHashSync } from '@stoneforge/quarry';

const hash = computeContentHashSync(element);
```

**Excluded from hash:**
- `id`
- `createdAt`
- `updatedAt`
- `createdBy`
- `contentHash`

### Merge Strategy

```typescript
import { mergeElements } from '@stoneforge/quarry';

// Third argument is TTL in milliseconds, not an options object.
const merged = mergeElements(local, remote, 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
```

The source of truth is `packages/quarry/src/sync/merge.ts`. Rules run in this order:

1. Identical content hashes keep the local element without a conflict.
2. `getTombstoneStatus()` recognizes a tombstone by a nonempty string `deletedAt`, not by `status` alone. It is fresh when `Date.now() - Date.parse(deletedAt) <= tombstoneTtl` (including the TTL boundary), and expired otherwise. An invalid date is classified as expired.
3. A fresh tombstone wins over live state; an expired tombstone loses to live state, regardless of `updatedAt` or closed status. These returns select the entire winner without tag union.
4. If both sides are tombstones, neither freshness nor `deletedAt` orders them: they fall through to status handling and last-write-wins below.
5. Status precedence applies when both `status` fields are strings: `closed` and `tombstone` are treated as closed states and beat a status outside that set. If both are in the set, neither gets precedence. This rule runs after tombstone TTL handling; a status-only `tombstone` without `deletedAt` is classified as live but still gets this status precedence. A status winner is returned without tag union.
6. Otherwise, later `updatedAt` wins, with local winning ties; tags are merged as a set union. For two normal tombstones (`status: "tombstone"` on both), this is the rule regardless of whether either has expired.

The TTL defaults to **30 days** in the numeric third parameter of `mergeElements()`. Direct callers can override it in milliseconds. `SyncService` import calls omit that parameter and use the default; there is no import option or YAML setting for this TTL. Expiry changes merge precedence, not export retention: it does not itself purge tombstones.

### Merge Resolution

| Scenario (after identical-hash check) | Winner |
|----------|--------|
| Fresh tombstone vs. live | Tombstone, even against closed live state |
| Expired tombstone vs. live | Live, regardless of timestamps |
| Both tombstones with normal tombstone statuses | Later `updatedAt`; local on ties; tags union |
| Both live, one closed-state status and one other string status | Closed-state version |
| No tombstone or status winner | Later `updatedAt`; local on ties; tags union |
| `force: true` import | Remote; bypasses `mergeElements()` |

Conflicts are tracked in `ImportResult.conflicts`.

---

## Backend Differences

| Feature | Bun | Node | Browser |
|---------|-----|------|---------|
| Native | Yes | No (FFI) | No (WASM) |
| Async required | No | No | Yes (OPFS) |
| Performance | Best | Good | Good |
| Memory | Low | Medium | Higher |

### Bun Backend

```typescript
import { BunStorageBackend } from '@stoneforge/storage/bun';

const backend = new BunStorageBackend({ path: './stoneforge.db' });
```

### Node Backend

```typescript
import { NodeStorageBackend } from '@stoneforge/storage/node';

const backend = new NodeStorageBackend({ path: './stoneforge.db' });
```

### Browser Backend

```typescript
import { BrowserStorageBackend } from '@stoneforge/storage/browser';

// Uses OPFS (Origin Private File System)
const backend = await BrowserStorageBackend.create({ path: './stoneforge.db' });
```

```typescript
import { mapStorageError, isConstraintError } from '@stoneforge/storage';

try {
  storage.run('INSERT ...');
} catch (err) {
  const mapped = mapStorageError(err);
  if (isConstraintError(mapped)) {
    // Handle constraint violation
  }
}
```

## Problem
The orchestrator server emits `MaxListenersExceededWarning` because event listeners accumulate without cleanup in the session manager's event forwarding.

## Root Cause
In `packages/orchestrator-sdk/src/runtime/session-manager.ts`, the `setupSessionEventForwarding()` method (around line 1196) attaches **7 event listeners** per spawned session (`event`, `pty-data`, `error`, `exit`, `stderr`, `raw`, and a **duplicate** `pty-data` at ~line 1287). These listeners are never explicitly removed when sessions terminate.

With Node.js's default max of 10 listeners, spawning just 2 concurrent sessions triggers the warning.

A secondary contributor is in `apps/orchestrator-server/src/services.ts` (~lines 164-176): the `onResultEvent` listener added per dispatched session is only removed when a 'result' event fires. If a session terminates without emitting 'result', the listener leaks.

## What to Do
1. **Remove the duplicate `pty-data` listener** (~line 1287 in session-manager.ts)
2. **Add cleanup** in `setupSessionEventForwarding()`: return a cleanup function that calls `.off()` for all attached listeners, and call it when the session exits/terminates
3. **Fix the `onResultEvent` leak** in services.ts: ensure the listener is removed on session exit, not just on 'result' event
4. **Do NOT just increase `setMaxListeners()`** — that masks the leak. Fix the root cause.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Background

Task el-3hg6 changed the dispatch daemon to skip director roles during inbox forwarding. The code is merged but the documentation was never updated to reflect this behavior change.

## Required Changes

### 1. `docs/ORCHESTRATION_PLAN.md` (around lines 210-216)

**Current:**
```markdown
**Process for Persistent Workers and Directors:**
1. Poll for unread messages in inbox
2. For each unread message:
   - Check if agent has active session
   - **If active session:** Forward message to session as user input
   - **If no active session:** Message waits until session starts
3. Mark forwarded messages as read
```

**Change to:**
```markdown
**Process for Persistent Workers:**
1. Poll for unread messages in inbox
2. For each unread message:
   - Check if agent has active session
   - **If active session:** Forward message to session as user input
   - **If no active session:** Message waits until session starts
3. Mark forwarded messages as read

**Process for Directors:**
Directors are **skipped** by the dispatch daemon's inbox polling. Messages remain unread in the director's inbox until the director explicitly checks them at natural breakpoints (e.g., \`el inbox <director-id>\`). This prevents interrupting the director's workflow with unsolicited messages injected as user input.
```

### 2. `docs/reference/orchestrator-services.md` (around lines 346-348)

**Current:**
```markdown
For persistent workers and directors:
- Active session = forward message as user input
- No active session = message waits
```

**Change to:**
```markdown
For persistent workers:
- Active session = forward message as user input
- No active session = message waits

For directors:
- Messages are **not forwarded** — directors are skipped by inbox polling
- Messages remain unread until the director checks its inbox manually
```

- Both files updated as described above
- No other changes needed — this is a docs-only task

## Bug

The ActiveAgentCard on the Activity page displays "> idle..." even when an agent is actively executing tools. This happens because events without text content (e.g. tool_use events) are filtered out before reaching the card.

## Root Cause

In `apps/orchestrator-web/src/api/hooks/useActiveAgentOutputs.ts` (line ~44), the hook skips events where `!event.content`:

```typescript
if (!event.agentId || !event.content) continue;
```

Many agent events (tool_use, some tool_result, system events) have no `message` text, so they get filtered. When an agent starts a session and immediately uses tools before emitting any text, `lastOutput` stays undefined, and the card falls through to the "> idle..." fallback in `ActiveAgentCard.tsx`.

## Fix

Two complementary changes:

### 1. Show tool activity in useActiveAgentOutputs (`apps/orchestrator-web/src/api/hooks/useActiveAgentOutputs.ts`)
- When an event has no `content` but has a `type` of `tool_use` or `tool_result`, generate a synthetic display string (e.g. "Using Bash...", "Tool completed")
- Use `event.tool` name if available for more descriptive output
- Always update the map entry timestamp so the card knows the agent is active

### 2. Add "working" fallback in ActiveAgentCard (`apps/orchestrator-web/src/components/activity/ActiveAgentCard.tsx`)
- When `lastOutput` is undefined but the session status is `running`, show "> working..." instead of "> idle..."
- Keep "> idle..." only for when the session is truly idle (status is `idle` or `suspended`)

## Key Files
- `apps/orchestrator-web/src/api/hooks/useActiveAgentOutputs.ts` — event filtering logic
- `apps/orchestrator-web/src/components/activity/ActiveAgentCard.tsx` — display fallback logic
- `apps/orchestrator-server/src/routes/events.ts` — SSE event streaming (maps `event.message` to `content`)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Agent card shows tool activity (e.g. "> Using Bash...") when agent is executing tools
- Agent card shows "> working..." when session is running but no output received yet
- Agent card still shows "> idle..." only when session is genuinely idle
- No regressions in existing activity page behavior

## Problem

When a merge steward hands off a task (via `el task handoff`), the task stays in `status=REVIEW` with `mergeStatus=testing`. This makes the task invisible to the worker dispatch daemon (`api.ready()` only returns OPEN/IN_PROGRESS tasks) but still visible to the merge steward (`getTasksAwaitingMerge()` queries REVIEW + pending/testing). The stuck merge recovery then resets mergeStatus to pending, and the steward picks it up again — creating an infinite loop where no worker ever acts on the review feedback.

## Root Cause

`handoffTask()` in `task-assignment-service.ts:559-636` only clears `assignee` and updates metadata. It does NOT change `task.status` or `mergeStatus`. The task stays in REVIEW, which workers never see.

## Required Changes

In `packages/orchestrator-sdk/src/services/task-assignment-service.ts`, modify `handoffTask()` (line 632) to also set:
- `status: TaskStatus.OPEN` — so `api.ready()` returns it and the dispatch daemon assigns it to a worker
- `mergeStatus: undefined` (or remove it) in the orchestrator metadata — so the merge steward does NOT pick it up

The update call at line 632 should change from:
```typescript
return this.api.update<Task>(taskId, {
  assignee: undefined,
  metadata: newMeta,
});
```

To something like:
```typescript
return this.api.update<Task>(taskId, {
  assignee: undefined,
  status: TaskStatus.OPEN,
  metadata: newMeta, // with mergeStatus cleared
});
```

And the `metaUpdates` block (lines 611-622) should include `mergeStatus: undefined`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- After a steward calls `el task handoff`, the task has `status=OPEN` and no `mergeStatus` (or a value the steward ignores)
- The dispatch daemon's `pollWorkerAvailability()` picks up the handed-off task and assigns it to a worker
- The merge steward's `getTasksAwaitingMerge()` does NOT return handed-off tasks
- Existing worker-to-worker handoff behavior is unaffected (worker handoffs already happen on IN_PROGRESS tasks, which is fine)
- Update existing tests in `task-assignment-service.test.ts` (the `handoffTask` describe block starting around line 305) to assert the new status and mergeStatus
- All tests pass: `bun test src` from `packages/orchestrator-sdk`
- `npx turbo run typecheck` passes

- `packages/orchestrator-sdk/src/services/task-assignment-service.ts` — `handoffTask()` method (lines 559-636)
- `packages/orchestrator-sdk/src/services/task-assignment-service.test.ts` — handoff tests (line 305+)

## Goal
Add HTTP API routes to orchestrator-server for browsing, reading, writing, and searching workspace files. The server runs locally and has full filesystem access — these routes replace the browser's File System Access API.

## Context
The editor currently uses the browser's File System Access API (FSAPI) to read/write local files. FSAPI is Chromium-only and can't support LSP module resolution. We're migrating to server-side filesystem access so the editor works in all browsers and can support a server-side TypeScript LSP.

The orchestrator-server already runs on the local machine with a known workspace root. It uses the Hono framework. See existing routes in `apps/orchestrator-server/src/routes/` for patterns.

## Routes to Add

Create a new route file: `apps/orchestrator-server/src/routes/workspace-files.ts`

### 1. `GET /api/workspace/tree`
Returns the recursive directory tree of the workspace.

Query params:
- `root` (optional) — subdirectory path relative to workspace root, defaults to `'.'`
- `depth` (optional) — max recursion depth, defaults to `10`

Response: `{ entries: FileEntry[] }`
```ts
interface FileEntry {
  name: string;        // filename
  path: string;        // relative path from workspace root
  type: 'file' | 'directory';
  size?: number;       // bytes, files only
  lastModified?: number; // unix timestamp ms
  children?: FileEntry[]; // directories only
}
```

Must skip ignored directories: `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, `.next`, `coverage`, `__pycache__`, `.vscode`, `.idea`, `.DS_Store`, `.elemental-worktrees`. Use a constant array for the ignore list.

Use `fs.readdir` with `withFileTypes: true` for efficient directory scanning. Sort: directories first, then alphabetical.

### 2. `GET /api/workspace/file`
Reads a single file's content.

Query params:
- `path` (required) — file path relative to workspace root

Response: `{ content: string, name: string, path: string, size: number, lastModified: number }`

**Security:** Validate that the resolved path is within the workspace root (prevent path traversal with `../`). Return 400 for paths outside the workspace. Return 404 if file doesn't exist. Return 413 if file exceeds 5MB.

### 3. `PUT /api/workspace/file`
Writes content to a file.

Body: `{ path: string, content: string }`

Response: `{ success: true, path: string, bytesWritten: number }`

**Security:** Same path traversal protection as read. Create parent directories if they don't exist (`fs.mkdir recursive`).

### 4. `POST /api/workspace/search`
Searches file contents across the workspace. This replaces the client-side file-by-file search.

Body:
```ts
{
  query: string;          // search string
  isRegex?: boolean;      // treat query as regex
  caseSensitive?: boolean;
  wholeWord?: boolean;
  includePattern?: string; // glob pattern for files to include
  excludePattern?: string; // glob pattern for files to exclude
  maxResults?: number;     // default 200
}
```

Response:
```ts
{
  results: Array<{
    path: string;
    matches: Array<{
      line: number;
      column: number;
      length: number;
      lineContent: string;  // the full line text
    }>;
  }>;
  totalMatches: number;
  truncated: boolean;  // true if maxResults was hit
}
```

Implementation: Walk the directory tree, skip ignored dirs and binary files, read text files and search line by line. Skip files over 1MB. Limit matches per file to 20.

### 5. Route registration
Register the new routes in `apps/orchestrator-server/src/index.ts` alongside the existing route registrations.

## Determining the workspace root
The server needs to know the workspace root path. Check how the server is initialized — look at the server config/context for a workspace path or cwd. If none exists, use `process.cwd()` as the workspace root. Store it on the Hono context or in a shared config so routes can access it.

## Goal
Add server-side language servers that communicate with the Monaco editor over WebSocket. This gives the editor real LSP features: module resolution, go-to-definition, hover types, diagnostics, and autocompletion — all with full filesystem access. Support multiple languages via a pluggable architecture.

## Context
The editor currently relies on Monaco's built-in TypeScript worker, which only knows about files loaded as editor models. It can't resolve imports because it has no filesystem access. By running language servers on the orchestrator-server and bridging them to the browser via WebSocket, the LSP gets full access to the workspace, node_modules, tsconfig.json, etc.

The Vite dev server already proxies /ws to the orchestrator-server (see apps/orchestrator-web/vite.config.ts line 28-32).

## Supported Language Servers

Build a pluggable architecture that supports multiple language servers. Each server is defined by a config object:

```ts
interface LanguageServerConfig {
  id: string;                    // e.g., 'typescript', 'python', 'rust'
  name: string;                  // display name
  command: string;               // binary to spawn
  args: string[];                // command arguments
  languages: string[];           // Monaco language IDs this server handles
  /** Check if this server's toolchain is installed */
  isAvailable: () => Promise<boolean>;
}
```

### Language servers to include:

1. **TypeScript/JavaScript** — `typescript-language-server --stdio`
   - Languages: typescript, javascript, typescriptreact, javascriptreact
   - Availability: check for typescript-language-server in PATH or node_modules/.bin
   - Install: pnpm add -D typescript-language-server typescript in orchestrator-server

2. **Python** — `pyright-langserver --stdio` (Pyright is faster and more reliable than pylsp)
   - Languages: python
   - Availability: check for pyright-langserver in PATH (pip install pyright)
   - Don't install — check availability at runtime and skip gracefully if not found

3. **Rust** — `rust-analyzer`
   - Languages: rust
   - Availability: check for rust-analyzer in PATH (rustup component add rust-analyzer)
   - Don't install — check availability at runtime

4. **Go** — `gopls serve`
   - Languages: go
   - Availability: check for gopls in PATH (go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest)
   - Don't install — check availability at runtime

5. **CSS/HTML/JSON** — vscode-css-languageserver --stdio, vscode-html-languageserver --stdio, vscode-json-languageserver --stdio
   - Languages: css/scss/less, html, json/jsonc
   - These are npm packages: vscode-langservers-extracted
   - Install: pnpm add -D vscode-langservers-extracted in orchestrator-server
   - Availability: always (installed as dependency)

For servers that aren't installed (Python, Rust, Go), the system should **gracefully degrade** — no LSP features for those languages, no errors. Log which servers are available at startup.

## Implementation

### 1. Server-side: Language server manager
**File:** apps/orchestrator-server/src/services/lsp-manager.ts

Create a manager that spawns and manages language server child processes:
- Registry of LanguageServerConfig entries
- On startup (or on first request), check which servers are available
- Spawn server processes on demand (when a file of that language is first opened)
- Each server communicates over stdio using LSP (JSON-RPC with Content-Length headers)
- Handle lifecycle: start, stop, restart on crash
- One instance per language server (each serves all files of its languages)
- Expose a method: getServerForLanguage(languageId: string): ChildProcess | null

### 2. Server-side: WebSocket-to-LSP bridge
**File:** apps/orchestrator-server/src/routes/lsp-websocket.ts (or extend existing websocket.ts)

Add a WebSocket endpoint at /ws/lsp:
- Client connects with a query param specifying the language: /ws/lsp?language=typescript
- Look up the appropriate language server via the manager
- Forward messages bidirectionally:
  - WebSocket -> prepend Content-Length header -> language server stdin
  - Language server stdout -> strip Content-Length header -> WebSocket
- Handle disconnection: keep the language server running (it can serve multiple reconnects)
- Return an error if no server is available for the requested language

### 3. Server-side: LSP status endpoint

GET /api/lsp/status

Response:
```ts
{
  servers: Array<{
    id: string;
    name: string;
    languages: string[];
    available: boolean;     // is the binary installed?

  }>;
```

In the editor's onMount callback:

**Current behavior:** When opening a new file, the code searches for ANY tab with `isPreview && !isDirty` to replace. This means it might replace a tab that isn't the currently active one, which is confusing.

**Desired behavior:** When opening a new file:
- If the **currently active** tab is not dirty → replace it with the new file
- If the currently active tab IS dirty → open the new file in a new tab
- The `isPreview` flag should NOT be used for this logic. What matters is whether the active tab is dirty or not.

**File:** `apps/orchestrator-web/src/routes/editor/index.tsx`

There are THREE places where tabs are created/replaced — all need the same fix:

### 3a. Document loading useEffect (~line 263-303)
Replace:
```tsx
// Find preview tab to replace
const previewIndex = prevTabs.findIndex(t => t.isPreview && !t.isDirty);
```
With logic that finds the currently active tab and checks if it's dirty:
```tsx
// Replace the active tab if it's not dirty
const activeIndex = prevTabs.findIndex(t => t.id === activeTabId);
if (activeIndex !== -1 && !prevTabs[activeIndex].isDirty) {
  const updated = [...prevTabs];
  updated[activeIndex] = newTab;
  return updated;
}
```

Note: `activeTabId` needs to be accessible in this closure. It's referenced from the component scope, so it should be in the useEffect dependency array (or use a ref).

### 3b. handleSelectFile for workspace files (~line 343-358)
Same change — replace the preview tab logic:
```tsx
setTabs(prevTabs => {
  if (pinTab) {
    return [...prevTabs, newTab];
  }
  // Replace the active tab if it's not dirty
  const activeIndex = prevTabs.findIndex(t => t.id === activeTabId);
  if (activeIndex !== -1 && !prevTabs[activeIndex].isDirty) {
    const updated = [...prevTabs];
    updated[activeIndex] = newTab;
    return updated;
  }
  return [...prevTabs, newTab];
});
```

### 3c. Search result navigation (~line 417-426)
Same pattern for when opening a file from search results.

### 3d. Remove isPreview from new tab creation
Since we no longer use `isPreview` for tab replacement, set `isPreview: false` on all new tabs (or remove the field usage). The italic styling for preview tabs can be removed too — the new behavior doesn't distinguish preview vs pinned tabs.

- Switch to another tab → X disappears on the previous tab, appears on the new active tab
- Active tab has a blue top border, inactive tabs have standard border color

- Open file A → type something → open file B → B opens in a new tab (A stays because it's dirty)

## Problem
The MonacoLanguageClient in `apps/orchestrator-web/src/lib/monaco-lsp/lsp-client.ts` does not send `rootUri` or `workspaceFolders` in the LSP initialize request. Additionally, `apps/orchestrator-web/tsconfig.json` lacks `paths` mappings for `@elemental/*` packages, so even with rootUri the TS language server can't resolve local module imports.

## Root Causes

### 1. Missing rootUri in LSP initialize request
- `connectLsp()` in `lsp-client.ts:157-164` creates MonacoLanguageClient without rootUri/workspaceFolders
- The comment on line 161 says "rootUri is set via the LSP initialize request by the server" — this is backwards, the CLIENT must tell the server
- The workspace root IS available from `/api/lsp/status` (`LspStatusResponse.workspaceRoot`) — it's fetched but never used

### 2. Missing tsconfig paths in orchestrator-web
- `apps/orchestrator-web/tsconfig.json` does NOT define `compilerOptions.paths` for `@elemental/*`
- It does NOT extend `../../tsconfig.base.json` (unlike `apps/orchestrator-server/tsconfig.json` which does)
- When the TS language server opens a web app file, it finds this tsconfig and can't resolve `@elemental/core`, `@elemental/sdk`, etc.
- Compare with `apps/orchestrator-server/tsconfig.json` which has full path mappings and works correctly
- At build time Vite handles resolution via its own module resolution, so this gap only manifests in the LSP

## What to Fix

### Fix A: Send rootUri in LSP initialize request
1. In `connectLsp()` (lsp-client.ts), fetch the workspace root from the already-cached `fetchLspStatus()` response
2. Pass `rootUri` (as a `file://` URI) and `workspaceFolders` in the MonacoLanguageClient `clientOptions`
3. Format: `workspaceFolders: [{ uri: 'file:///path/to/workspace', name: 'elemental' }]`

### Fix B: Add paths to orchestrator-web tsconfig.json
Add `@elemental/*` path mappings to `apps/orchestrator-web/tsconfig.json`:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "paths": {
      "@elemental/core": ["../../packages/core/src/index.ts"],
      "@elemental/core/*": ["../../packages/core/src/*"],
      "@elemental/storage": ["../../packages/storage/src/index.ts"],
      "@elemental/storage/*": ["../../packages/storage/src/*"],
      "@elemental/sdk": ["../../packages/sdk/src/index.ts"],
      "@elemental/sdk/*": ["../../packages/sdk/src/*"],
      "@elemental/orchestrator-sdk": ["../../packages/orchestrator-sdk/src/index.ts"],
      "@elemental/orchestrator-sdk/*": ["../../packages/orchestrator-sdk/src/*"],
      "@elemental/ui": ["../../packages/ui/src/index.ts"],
      "@elemental/ui/*": ["../../packages/ui/src/*"],
      "@elemental/shared-routes": ["../../packages/shared-routes/src/index.ts"],
      "@elemental/shared-routes/*": ["../../packages/shared-routes/src/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

Use `apps/orchestrator-server/tsconfig.json` as reference for which packages to include. Check `apps/orchestrator-web/package.json` dependencies to see which `@elemental/*` packages are actually used.

**IMPORTANT:** Verify that adding paths does not break `npx turbo run typecheck`. The web app uses `"moduleResolution": "bundler"` which may interact differently with paths than other apps. Run typecheck after the change.

## Problem
The LSP status icon in the editor header shows gray (not connected) because the external LSP never connects. Additionally, running Monaco's built-in TypeScript worker alongside the external LSP causes duplicate completions and hover info.

## Root Causes

### 1. Monaco Ref Timing Bug — LSP never connects
In `LspMonacoEditor.tsx:136-137`, the `useLsp` hook is called with:
```tsx
const { state: lspState } = useLsp({
  monaco: monacoRef.current ?? undefined,  // Always undefined on first render!
  ...
});
```

`monacoRef.current` is only set later in `handleMount` (line 152). Since it's a ref (not state), changing it doesn't trigger a re-render, so the hook never sees the Monaco instance. The auto-connect logic in `use-lsp.ts:158` checks `!monacoInstance` and bails out.

### 2. Dual Language Services — duplicate results when LSP connects
Monaco merges providers from multiple sources. With both the built-in TS worker AND external LSP active:
- **Completions**: Every autocomplete item appears twice in the dropdown
- **Hover**: Overlapping hover info from both sources
- **Diagnostics**: Separate "owner" strings so they coexist (no visual duplication)
- **Definitions, references, etc.**: All duplicated

### 3. No Disconnect Detection
When the WebSocket closes (`lsp-client.ts:184-189`), the `activeClients` map is cleaned up but nothing notifies the React hook. The sync effect in `use-lsp.ts:185-192` only runs when its dependencies change, which doesn't happen on socket close.

## What to Fix

### Part A: Fix Monaco instance timing
1. In `LspMonacoEditor.tsx`: Convert the Monaco instance from a ref to state (or add a state trigger alongside the ref) so that when `handleMount` fires, the component re-renders and `useLsp` receives the actual Monaco instance
2. Ensure no infinite re-render loops

### Part B: Disable built-in TS features when LSP is connected
Use `setModeConfiguration()` to selectively disable Monaco's built-in TypeScript features when the external LSP takes over. This avoids duplicate completions, hover, etc.

```typescript
// When LSP connects for a TS/JS language:
const defaults = monaco.languages.typescript.typescriptDefaults; // or javascriptDefaults
defaults.setModeConfiguration({
  completionItems: false,
  hovers: false,
  diagnostics: false,
  definitions: false,
  references: false,
  documentHighlights: false,
  rename: false,
  codeActions: false,
  signatureHelp: false,
  // Keep these for basic editor UX
  selectionRanges: true,
  foldingRanges: true,
});
```

**IMPORTANT behavioral requirements:**
- Only disable built-in features when LSP is CONNECTED for that language
- If LSP disconnects or is unavailable, RE-ENABLE built-in features as fallback
- Apply to both `typescriptDefaults` and `javascriptDefaults` as appropriate based on the file language
- This should be done in a useEffect that reacts to `lspState` changes

### Part C: Fix disconnect detection
Add a mechanism to detect WebSocket disconnects promptly. Options:
- A polling interval (e.g., every 3-5 seconds check `getLspConnectionState`)
- Or add a subscription/callback mechanism to `lsp-client.ts` that the hook listens to for connection state changes

This is important because Part B needs to re-enable built-in features on disconnect.

## Key Files
- `apps/orchestrator-web/src/components/editor/LspMonacoEditor.tsx` — fix Monaco instance timing + add setModeConfiguration
- `apps/orchestrator-web/src/lib/monaco-lsp/use-lsp.ts` — fix disconnect detection
- `apps/orchestrator-web/src/lib/monaco-lsp/lsp-client.ts` — optionally add connection state change callbacks

## Acceptance Criteria
- When opening a TypeScript file, the LSP status icon turns green (connected) within a few seconds
- Autocomplete dropdown shows each item only ONCE (no duplicates from dual providers)
- Hover info appears once (not duplicated)
- If the WebSocket disconnects, the icon changes from green to gray/red within 5 seconds AND built-in TS features are re-enabled
- If LSP is unavailable for a language, built-in features remain active as fallback
- No infinite re-render loops from the state change
- The editor still renders and works correctly while LSP is connecting

## Problem
`monaco-languageclient` v10.x (and v8.x) requires `@codingame/monaco-vscode-api` service initialization which is incompatible with `@monaco-editor/react`. The `initialize()` call from `@codingame/monaco-vscode-api` replaces Monaco's internal service registry, which causes the `@monaco-editor/react` editor component to unmount and lose state. This cannot be fixed by timing the initialization earlier — the two systems are fundamentally incompatible.

## Solution
Replace `MonacoLanguageClient` with a **lightweight LSP client** that:
1. Uses `vscode-ws-jsonrpc` (already installed, no VSCode dependency) for JSON-RPC over WebSocket
2. Manually registers Monaco language providers (completion, hover, diagnostics, definitions)
3. Translates between LSP protocol messages and Monaco's provider interfaces
4. Works with vanilla `monaco-editor` and `@monaco-editor/react` without any `@codingame/monaco-vscode-*` packages

## Architecture

### WebSocket Layer (keep existing)
- `vscode-ws-jsonrpc` provides `WebSocketMessageReader`/`WebSocketMessageWriter` — reuse these
- Keep the existing `getLspWebSocketUrl()` and WebSocket connection logic from `lsp-client.ts`

### JSON-RPC Layer
Use `vscode-jsonrpc` (dependency of `vscode-ws-jsonrpc`) to create a `MessageConnection`:
```typescript
import { createMessageConnection } from 'vscode-jsonrpc';
import { WebSocketMessageReader, WebSocketMessageWriter, toSocket } from 'vscode-ws-jsonrpc';

const webSocket = new WebSocket(url);
const socket = toSocket(webSocket);
const reader = new WebSocketMessageReader(socket);
const writer = new WebSocketMessageWriter(socket);
const connection = createMessageConnection(reader, writer);
connection.listen();
```

### LSP Protocol Layer
Use `vscode-languageserver-protocol` (already installed as transitive dep) for typed LSP request/notification types:
```typescript
import {
  InitializeRequest, InitializeParams,
  CompletionRequest, CompletionParams,
  HoverRequest, HoverParams,
  DidOpenTextDocumentNotification,
  DidChangeTextDocumentNotification,
  PublishDiagnosticsNotification,
  // etc.
} from 'vscode-languageserver-protocol';
```

### Monaco Provider Registration
Register providers with Monaco directly. Map LSP responses to Monaco's format:

1. **Diagnostics**: Listen for `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` notification, convert to `monaco.editor.setModelMarkers()`
2. **Completion**: Register `monaco.languages.registerCompletionItemProvider()`, send `textDocument/completion` request
3. **Hover**: Register `monaco.languages.registerHoverProvider()`, send `textDocument/hover` request
4. **Go to Definition**: Register `monaco.languages.registerDefinitionProvider()`, send `textDocument/definition` request

### Document Sync
Track open documents and send `textDocument/didOpen` and `textDocument/didChange` notifications to the language server when editor content changes.

### Step 1: Create lightweight LSP client module
Create `apps/orchestrator-web/src/lib/monaco-lsp/lightweight-client.ts`:
- Initialize LSP connection (JSON-RPC over WebSocket)
- Send `initialize` request with proper `rootUri` and `workspaceFolders` (from workspace root fetched via `/api/lsp/status`)
- Send `initialized` notification
- Handle `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` notification → convert to Monaco markers
- Implement `textDocument/completion` → Monaco completion provider
- Implement `textDocument/hover` → Monaco hover provider
- Send `textDocument/didOpen` and `textDocument/didChange` notifications

## LSP ↔ Monaco Type Conversion Reference

### Diagnostics (server → client push)
```typescript
// LSP Diagnostic → Monaco IMarkerData
function toMonacoMarker(diagnostic: Diagnostic): monaco.editor.IMarkerData {
  return {
    severity: toMonacoSeverity(diagnostic.severity),
    message: diagnostic.message,
    startLineNumber: diagnostic.range.start.line + 1,  // LSP is 0-based, Monaco is 1-based
    startColumn: diagnostic.range.start.character + 1,
    endLineNumber: diagnostic.range.end.line + 1,
    endColumn: diagnostic.range.end.character + 1,
    source: diagnostic.source,
    code: typeof diagnostic.code === 'number' ? String(diagnostic.code) : diagnostic.code,
  };
}
```

### Completion (client → server request)
```typescript
// Monaco Position → LSP CompletionParams
const params: CompletionParams = {
  textDocument: { uri: model.uri.toString() },
  position: { line: position.lineNumber - 1, character: position.column - 1 },
};
// LSP CompletionItem → Monaco CompletionItem conversion needed
```

### Hover (client → server request)
```typescript
// LSP Hover → Monaco Hover
const params: HoverParams = {
  textDocument: { uri: model.uri.toString() },
  position: { line: position.lineNumber - 1, character: position.column - 1 },
};
```

## Context

To install extensions from OpenVSX, we need to parse VSIX files (ZIP archives containing extension code and metadata) and filter to only declarative extensions (themes, grammars, snippets) that are safe to load without a full extension host.

## What to Do

### New file: `apps/orchestrator-web/src/lib/openvsx/vsix-parser.ts`

1. Add `jszip` dependency to `apps/orchestrator-web/package.json`
2. Create a `parseVsix(buffer: ArrayBuffer)` function that:
   - Unzips the VSIX using jszip
   - Reads `extension/package.json` to get the manifest
   - Extracts files referenced in `contributes.themes`, `contributes.grammars`, `contributes.snippets`
   - Returns a structured result: `{ manifest, contributedFiles: Map<string, Uint8Array> }`

### Compatibility filter: `isDeclarativeExtension(manifest)`

Only allow installation if:
- No `main` or `browser` entry point (extension runs code → reject)
- `contributes` only contains supported keys: `themes`, `grammars`, `languages`, `snippets`, `iconThemes`, `productIconThemes`
- Reject if `contributes` contains: `commands`, `debuggers`, `views`, `menus`, `keybindings`, `taskDefinitions`, `webview*`, etc.
- Check `engines.vscode` — warn or reject if it requires an API version beyond what @codingame/monaco-vscode-api supports

### Export types

```typescript
interface ParsedExtension {
  manifest: ExtensionManifest;
  contributedFiles: Map<string, Uint8Array>;  // path → file contents
}

interface ExtensionManifest {
  name: string;
  publisher: string;
  version: string;
  displayName?: string;
  description?: string;
  categories?: string[];
  contributes?: ExtensionContributes;
  engines?: { vscode?: string };
  icon?: string;
}
```

## What to Do

### New file: `apps/orchestrator-web/src/lib/openvsx/storage.ts`

Create an IndexedDB storage layer with two object stores:

1. **`installed_extensions`** — stores extension manifests + metadata
   - Key: extension ID (`publisher.name`)
   - Value: `{ id, manifest, installedAt, version }`

2. **`extension_files`** — stores extracted files from the VSIX
   - Key: compound key `extensionId + "/" + filePath`
   - Value: file content (JSON parsed for .json files, string for others)

### API

```typescript
// Lifecycle
initExtensionStorage(): Promise<void>

// Extensions
saveExtension(id: string, manifest: ExtensionManifest, files: Map<string, Uint8Array>): Promise<void>
removeExtension(id: string): Promise<void>
getInstalledExtensions(): Promise<InstalledExtension[]>
getExtension(id: string): Promise<InstalledExtension | null>

// Files
getExtensionFile(extensionId: string, filePath: string): Promise<Uint8Array | null>
getExtensionFiles(extensionId: string): Promise<Map<string, Uint8Array>>
```
