title: CLI Reference: Core & Task Commands
content:
# CLI Reference: Core & Task Commands

Core CLI commands including global flags, CRUD operations, task management, and dependency commands.



## Global Flags

| Flag                       | Description                         |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `--help, -h`               | Show help                           |
| `--version, -V`            | Show version                        |
| `--json`                   | Output as JSON                      |
| `--quiet, -q`              | Minimal output (IDs only)           |
| `--verbose, -v`            | Enable debug output                 |
| `--actor <name>`           | Specify acting entity               |
| `--from <name>`            | Alias for `--actor`                 |
| `--db <path>`              | Override database path              |
| `--sign-key <key>`         | Private key for signing (base64 PKCS8) |
| `--sign-key-file <path>`   | Path to file containing private key |

## Environment Variables

| Variable          | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SF_ENTITY_ID`    | Entity ID for actor resolution. Automatically set in agent sessions. Used as fallback when `--actor` is not provided. Precedence: `--actor` flag > `SF_ENTITY_ID` > default (`el-0000`). |
| `STONEFORGE_ACTOR` | Actor name for identity resolution. Used by `sf whoami` and identity commands. Precedence: `--actor` flag > `STONEFORGE_ACTOR` > default. |

## Basic Commands

| Command         | Description                       |
| --------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `sf init`       | Initialize .stoneforge directory  |
| `sf help`       | Show help                         |
| `sf version`    | Show version                      |
| `sf stats`      | Show statistics                   |
| `sf whoami`     | Show current actor                |
| `sf serve`      | Start a Stoneforge server         |
| `sf completion` | Generate shell completion scripts |
| `sf alias`      | Show command aliases              |
| `sf install`    | Install stoneforge extensions     |
| `sf config`     | Manage configuration (show, set, unset, edit) |
| `sf identity`   | Manage identity settings (whoami, mode, sign, verify, keygen, hash) |
| `sf history`    | Show event history for an element |
| `sf log`        | Show operation log entries        |
| `sf metrics`    | Show provider usage metrics and costs |
| `sf gc`         | Garbage collect old ephemeral data |
| `sf doctor`     | Check system health and diagnose issues |
| `sf migrate`    | Run database migrations           |
| `sf sync`       | Sync commands (export, import, status) |
| `sf docs`       | Documentation infrastructure (init, add, dir) |
| `sf playbook`   | Manage playbooks (list, show, validate, create) |
| `sf reset`      | Reset workspace to clean state    |
| `sf merge`      | Squash-merge branch into main     |
| `sf agent`      | Manage orchestrator agents (list, show, register, start, stop, stream) |
| `sf daemon`     | Manage the dispatch daemon (start, stop, status, sleep, wake) |
| `sf dispatch`   | Dispatch a task to an agent       |
| `sf pool`       | Manage agent pools (list, show, create, update, delete, status, refresh) |
| `sf external-sync` | Manage external service sync (config, link, link-all, unlink, unlink-all, push, pull, sync, status, resolve) |

## CRUD Commands

| Command            | Description          |
| ------------------ | -------------------- |
| `sf create <type>` | Create a new element |
| `sf list [type]`   | List elements        |
| `sf show <id>`     | Show element details |
| `sf update <id>`   | Update element       |
| `sf delete <id>`   | Delete element       |
| `sf task create`   | Create task          |
| `sf task list`     | List tasks           |

#### create

```bash
sf create <type> [options]
```

| Option                    | Description                                   |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --title <text>`      | Title for the element (required for tasks)    |
| `-n, --name <text>`       | Alias for `--title`                           |
| `-d, --description <text>`| Task description (creates a linked document)  |
| `-p, --priority <1-5>`    | Priority level (1=critical, 5=minimal)        |
| `-c, --complexity <1-5>`  | Complexity level (1=trivial, 5=very complex)  |
| `--type <type>`           | Task type: bug, feature, task, chore          |
| `-a, --assignee <id>`     | Assignee entity ID                            |
| `--tag <tag>`             | Add a tag (can be repeated)                   |
| `--plan <id\|name>`       | Plan ID or name to attach this task to        |
| `--no-auto-link`          | Skip auto-linking to external provider even when configured |

```bash
sf create task --title "Fix login bug" --priority 1 --type bug
sf create task -t "New feature" --plan "My Plan Name"
sf create task -t "Internal task" --no-auto-link
```

#### list

```bash
sf list [type] [options]
```

| Option                  | Description                          |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `-t, --type <type>`     | Filter by element type               |
| `-s, --status <status>` | Filter by status (for tasks)         |
| `-p, --priority <1-5>`  | Filter by priority (for tasks)       |
| `-a, --assignee <id>`   | Filter by assignee (for tasks)       |
| `--tag <tag>`           | Filter by tag (can be repeated for AND) |
| `-l, --limit <n>`       | Maximum results (default: 50)        |
| `-o, --offset <n>`      | Skip first n results (for pagination) |

```bash
sf list task --status open
sf list task --priority 1 --limit 20
```

#### show

```bash
sf show <id> [options]
```

| Option                 | Description                              |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-e, --events`         | Include recent events/history            |
| `--events-limit <n>`   | Maximum events to show (default: 10)     |

```bash
sf show el-abc123
sf show el-abc123 --events
sf show el-abc123 --events --events-limit 20
sf show el-abc123 --json
sf show inbox-abc123     # Show inbox item with message content
```

#### update

```bash
sf update <id> [options]
```

| Option                  | Description                                        |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --title <text>`    | New title                                          |
| `-p, --priority <1-5>`  | New priority (tasks only)                          |
| `-c, --complexity <1-5>`| New complexity (tasks only)                        |
| `-s, --status <status>` | New status (tasks only: open, in_progress, blocked, deferred, backlog, review, closed, tombstone). Note: `blocked` is normally computed from dependencies; setting it directly via CLI is possible but not recommended. |
| `-a, --assignee <id>`   | New assignee (tasks only, empty string to unassign) |
| `-d, --description <text>` | Update description (tasks: updates linked doc; documents: updates content) |
| `--metadata <json>`     | JSON metadata to merge into element (null values remove keys) |
| `--tag <tag>`           | Replace all tags (can be repeated)                 |
| `--add-tag <tag>`       | Add a tag (can be repeated)                        |
| `--remove-tag <tag>`    | Remove a tag (can be repeated)                     |

```bash
sf update el-abc123 --title "New Title"
sf update el-abc123 --priority 1 --status in_progress
sf update el-abc123 -d "Updated description text"
sf update el-abc123 --metadata '{"key": "value"}'
sf update el-abc123 --add-tag urgent --add-tag frontend
sf update el-abc123 --remove-tag old-tag
sf update el-abc123 --assignee ""  # Unassign
```

#### delete

```bash
sf delete <id> [options]
```

| Option                | Description                              |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-r, --reason <text>` | Deletion reason (recorded in audit trail) |
| `-f, --force`         | Skip confirmation prompt (for scripts) |

Note: Messages cannot be deleted as they are immutable.

```bash
sf delete el-abc123 --reason "Duplicate entry"
```

## Init Command

Initialize a new Stoneforge workspace in the current directory.

```bash
sf init [options]
```

| Option                          | Description                                              |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--name <name>`                 | Workspace name (optional)                                |
| `--actor <name>`                | Default actor name                                       |
| `--preset <preset>`             | Workflow preset (`auto`, `review`, `approve`). Skips interactive prompt. |
| `--demo`                        | Enable demo mode. Configures all agents to use the free `opencode/minimax-m2.5-free` provider (no API keys required). |

Creates `.stoneforge/` with config, database, gitignore, and playbooks directory. Also registers default agents (director, 2 workers, merge steward). Re-running is safe (idempotent). If `.stoneforge/` exists but no database, it creates the database and imports from JSONL sync files.

```bash
sf init
```

## Stats Command

Show statistics about the Stoneforge workspace.

```bash
sf stats [options]
```

```bash
sf stats
```

## Serve Command

```bash
sf serve [quarry|smithy] [options]
```

| Option         | Description                          |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `-p, --port <port>` | Port to listen on                |
| `-H, --host <host>` | Host to bind to                  |
| `--no-open`    | Do not open browser automatically    |

```bash
sf serve quarry --port 8080
sf serve smithy
sf serve --no-open
```

## Completion Command

```bash
sf completion <shell>
```

| Argument | Description                          |
| -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `shell`  | Shell type: `bash`, `zsh`, or `fish` |

```bash
sf completion bash   # or: zsh, fish
```

## Alias Command

```bash
sf alias
```

**Built-in aliases:**

| Alias              | Maps to      |
| ------------------ | ------------ |
| `add`, `new`       | `create`     |
| `rm`, `remove`     | `delete`     |
| `ls`               | `list`       |
| `s`, `get`         | `show`       |
| `todo`, `tasks`    | `ready`      |
| `done`, `complete` | `close`      |
| `st`               | `status`     |
| `dep`              | `dependency` |
| `msg`              | `message`    |
| `doc`              | `document`   |

> **Warning: `sf done`/`sf close` vs `sf task complete` — these are NOT the same!**
>
> | Command | What it does |
> |---------|-------------|
> | `sf done <id>` / `sf close <id>` | **Closes/archives** a task — marks it as done, no merge request created |
> | `sf task complete <id>` | **Completes a task in the orchestration workflow** — sets status to `review`, clears assignee, and creates a merge request |
>
> **Note:** `complete` is currently an alias for `close` (not `task complete`). Running `sf complete <id>` closes/archives the task — it does NOT trigger a merge request. Use `sf task complete` to complete a task in the orchestration workflow.

**Plugin aliases** (available when the orchestrator plugin is loaded):

| Alias              | Maps to      |
| ------------------ | ------------ |
| `agents`           | `agent list` |
| `pools`            | `pool list`  |

## Install Command

```bash
sf install <subcommand> [options]
```

| Subcommand | Description                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `skills`   | Install Claude skills to `.claude/skills/` |

#### install skills

| Option          | Description                  |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `-f, --force`   | Overwrite existing skill files |

```bash
sf install skills
sf install skills --force
```

## Reset Command

Reset an Stoneforge workspace to a clean state.

```bash
sf reset [options]
```

By default, this command will:
- Stop any running daemon
- Remove the database (all entities, tasks, messages, etc.)
- Remove sync files (elements.jsonl, dependencies.jsonl)
- Remove all uploaded files (.stoneforge/uploads/)
- Remove all worktrees (.stoneforge/.worktrees/ directory)
- Prune git worktrees

Configuration files (.stoneforge/config.yaml) will be preserved.

With `--full`, this command will delete the entire `.stoneforge` folder (including config and worktrees) and reinitialize with default configuration.

| Option              | Description                              |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-f, --force`       | Skip confirmation prompt                 |
| `--full`            | Delete everything and reinitialize       |
| `-s, --server <url>`| Orchestrator server URL (default: http://localhost:3456) |

```bash
sf reset              # Interactive confirmation, preserve config
sf reset --force      # Skip confirmation, preserve config
sf reset --full       # Delete everything and reinitialize
sf reset --full -f    # Full reset without confirmation
```

## Task Commands

| Command                          | Description                        |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `sf task ready`                  | List ready (unblocked, open) tasks |
| `sf task blocked`                | List blocked tasks                 |
| `sf task backlog`                | List backlog tasks                 |
| `sf task activate <id>`          | Move a task from backlog to open   |
| `sf task close <id>`             | Close task                         |
| `sf task reopen <id>`            | Reopen task                        |
| `sf task show <id>`              | Show task details                  |
| `sf task update <id>`            | Update task fields                 |
| `sf task delete <id>`            | Delete task                        |
| `sf task assign <task> <entity>` | Assign task                        |
| `sf task defer <id>`             | Defer task                         |
| `sf task undefer <id>`           | Remove deferral                    |
| `sf task describe <id>`          | Set or show task description       |
| `sf task handoff <id>`           | Hand off task to another agent     |
| `sf task complete <id>`          | Complete task and create merge request |
| `sf task merge <id>`             | Squash-merge task branch and close |
| `sf task reject <id>`            | Mark merge as failed, reopen task  |
| `sf task sync <id>`              | Sync task branch with main         |
| `sf task merge-status <id> <status>` | Update task merge status       |
| `sf task set-owner <id> <director-id>` | Set the owning director for a task |

**Top-level convenience commands:** Common task operations are also available as top-level commands (without the `task` prefix):

| Top-level Command           | Equivalent                   |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `sf ready`                  | `sf task ready`              |
| `sf blocked`                | `sf task blocked`            |
| `sf backlog`                | `sf task backlog`            |
| `sf close <id>`             | `sf task close <id>`         |
| `sf reopen <id>`            | `sf task reopen <id>`        |
| `sf assign <task> <entity>` | `sf task assign <task> <entity>` |
| `sf defer <id>`             | `sf task defer <id>`         |
| `sf undefer <id>`           | `sf task undefer <id>`       |

#### task ready

List ready (unblocked, open) tasks.

| Option                 | Description                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-a, --assignee <id>`  | Filter by assignee                |
| `-p, --priority <1-5>` | Filter by priority                |
| `-t, --type <type>`    | Filter by task type (bug, feature, task, chore) |
| `-l, --limit <n>`      | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf task ready --assignee alice --priority 1
```

#### task backlog

List backlog tasks.

| Option                 | Description                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-p, --priority <1-5>` | Filter by priority                |
| `-l, --limit <n>`      | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf task backlog --priority 1
```

#### task blocked

List blocked tasks.

| Option                 | Description                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-a, --assignee <id>`  | Filter by assignee                |
| `-p, --priority <1-5>` | Filter by priority                |
| `-l, --limit <n>`      | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf task blocked --assignee alice
```

#### task close

Close a task.

| Option                | Description              |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `-r, --reason <text>` | Reason for closing       |

```bash
sf task close abc123 --reason "Fixed"
```

#### task reopen

Reopen a closed task.

| Option                 | Description                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `-m, --message <text>` | Message to append to task description        |

```bash
sf task reopen abc123 --message "Issue not fully resolved"
```

#### task assign

Assign a task to an entity.

| Option           | Description                       |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-u, --unassign` | Remove assignment instead         |

```bash
sf task assign abc123 worker-1
sf task assign abc123 worker-1 --unassign
```

#### task defer

Defer a task until a future date.

| Option             | Description                        |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| `--until <date>`   | Date to defer until (ISO format)   |

```bash
sf task defer abc123 --until 2025-06-01
sf task undefer abc123
```

#### task describe

Set or show a task's description. Descriptions are stored as versioned documents.

| Option                 | Description                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-c, --content <text>` | Description content (inline)                        |
| `-f, --file <path>`    | Read description from file                          |
| `-s, --show`           | Show current description instead of setting         |
| `--append`             | Append to existing description instead of replacing |

```bash
sf task describe el-abc123 --content "Implement the login feature"
sf task describe el-abc123 --file specs/login.md
sf task describe el-abc123 --show
```

#### task handoff

| Option                 | Description                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-m, --message <text>` | Handoff message with context and reason             |
| `-b, --branch <name>`  | Override branch to preserve                         |
| `-w, --worktree <path>` | Override worktree path to preserve                 |
| `-s, --sessionId <id>` | Session ID (defaults to current session)            |

```bash
sf task handoff el-abc123 --message "Completed API, need help with frontend"
```

#### task complete

> **Note:** This is NOT the same as `sf close` or `sf done`. See the [Alias Command](#alias-command) section for details on the distinction.

| Option                   | Description                                     |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --summary <text>`   | Summary of what was accomplished                |
| `-c, --commitHash <hash>` | Commit hash for the final commit               |
| `--no-mr`                | Skip merge request creation                     |
| `--mr-title <title>`     | Custom MR title (defaults to task title)        |
| `--mr-body <body>`       | Custom MR body                                  |
| `-b, --baseBranch <name>` | Base branch for MR (default: auto-detect from task targetBranch, then main) |

```bash
sf task complete el-abc123
sf task complete el-abc123 --summary "Implemented login feature"
```

#### task merge

| Option                 | Description                     |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `-s, --summary <text>` | Summary of the merge           |

```bash
sf task merge el-abc123 --summary "All tests passing"
```

#### task reject

| Option                 | Description                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `-r, --reason <text>`  | Reason for rejection (required)              |
| `-m, --message <text>` | Handoff message for the next worker          |

```bash
sf task reject el-abc123 --reason "Tests failed" --message "Fix flaky test"
```

#### task sync

```bash
sf task sync el-abc123
sf task sync el-abc123 --json
```

#### task merge-status

Update the merge status of a task. Valid: `pending`, `testing`, `merging`, `merged`, `conflict`, `test_failed`, `failed`, `not_applicable`, `awaiting_approval`

| Option      | Description                                                                                         |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--force, -f` | Bypass merge verification when source branch is deleted and merge cannot be verified              |

**Safety verification for `merged` status:** When setting status to `merged`, the command verifies that the task's source branch has no commits ahead of `origin/{targetBranch}`. If unmerged commits are found, the command refuses with an actionable error suggesting `sf task merge` or `not_applicable`. Verification is skipped for local-only workspaces (no remote) and tasks without branch metadata.

**Deleted branch handling:** If the source branch has been deleted, the command attempts to verify the merge via the recorded merge commit hash (`mergeCommitHash` in orchestrator metadata). If the commit hash exists and is an ancestor of the target branch, verification passes. If no commit hash is available or it's not on the target, the command fails with an error. Use `--force` to override this check in legitimate edge cases.

```bash
sf task merge-status el-abc123 merged
sf task merge-status el-abc123 merged --force
sf task merge-status el-abc123 pending
sf task merge-status el-abc123 test_failed
```

#### task set-owner

Set the owning director for a task. This sets the `owningDirector` field in the task's orchestrator metadata, which is used for message routing in multi-director workspaces.

```bash
sf task set-owner el-abc123 el-dir01
```

#### task list

List tasks with optional filtering.

| Option                  | Description                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --status <status>` | Filter by status                                                                                                             |
| `--ready`               | Show only dispatch-ready tasks (accounts for blocked cache, draft plans, scheduled-for-future, ephemeral workflows, and plan-level blocking). Mutually exclusive with `--status`. |
| `-t, --type <type>`     | Filter by element type (bug, feature, task, chore)                                                                           |
| `-p, --priority <1-5>`  | Filter by priority                                                                                                           |
| `-a, --assignee <id>`   | Filter by assignee                                                                                                           |
| `--tag <tag>`           | Filter by tag (can be repeated for AND logic)                                                                                |
| `-l, --limit <n>`       | Maximum results (default: 50)                                                                                                |
| `-o, --offset <n>`      | Skip first n results (for pagination)                                                                                        |

```bash
sf task list --status open
sf task list --ready --assignee alice
sf task list --tag frontend --limit 20
```

## Dependency Commands

| Command                   | Description          |
| ------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `sf dependency add`       | Add dependency       |
| `sf dependency remove`    | Remove dependency    |
| `sf dependency list <id>` | List dependencies    |
| `sf dependency tree <id>` | Show dependency tree |

```bash
sf dependency add --type=blocks A B
sf dependency remove A B --type=blocks
sf dependency list abc123 -d out     # Outgoing
sf dependency list abc123 -d in      # Incoming
sf dependency list abc123 -d both    # Both
sf dependency tree abc123
```

#### dependency add

| Option                 | Description                                           |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --type <type>`    | Dependency type (required): blocks, parent-child, awaits, relates-to, references, supersedes, duplicates, caused-by, validates, mentions, authored-by, assigned-to, approved-by, replies-to |
| `-m, --metadata <json>` | JSON metadata to attach to the dependency            |

```bash
sf dependency add --type=blocks A B
```

**Semantics:** `sf dependency add --type=blocks A B` means A (blocked) is blocked BY B (blocker).

#### dependency list

| Option                    | Description                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `-t, --type <type>`       | Filter by dependency type                        |
| `-d, --direction <dir>`   | Direction: out, in, or both (default: both)      |

```bash
sf dependency list abc123 -d in --type blocks
```

#### dependency tree

| Option              | Description                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-d, --depth <n>`   | Maximum tree depth (default: 5)   |

```bash
sf dependency tree abc123
sf dependency tree abc123 --depth 3
```

## History Command

Show event history/timeline for an element.

```bash
sf history <id> [options]
```

| Option                  | Description                                              |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-l, --limit <n>`       | Maximum events to show (default: 50)                    |
| `-t, --type <type>`     | Filter by event type (created, updated, closed, reopened, deleted, dependency_added, dependency_removed) |
| `-a, --actor <actor>`   | Filter by actor                                          |
| `--after <time>`        | Show events after this timestamp (ISO 8601)              |
| `--before <time>`       | Show events before this timestamp (ISO 8601)             |
| `-f, --format <fmt>`    | Output format: timeline or table (default: timeline)     |

```bash
sf history el-abc123
sf history el-abc123 --limit 10
sf history el-abc123 --type updated
sf history el-abc123 --actor user:alice
sf history el-abc123 --format table
sf history el-abc123 --after 2024-01-01
```

## Log Command

Show persistent operation log entries for system observability.

```bash
sf log [options]
```

| Option                    | Description                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--level <level>`         | Filter by level: info, warn, error                                |
| `-c, --category <cat>`    | Filter by category: dispatch, merge, session, rate-limit, steward, recovery |
| `-s, --since <time>`      | Show entries since time (e.g., 2h, 30m, 1d, 1w) or ISO 8601      |
| `-t, --task <id>`         | Filter by task ID                                                 |
| `-a, --agent <id>`        | Filter by agent ID                                                |
| `-l, --limit <n>`         | Maximum entries to show (default: 20)                             |

```bash
sf log
sf log --level error
sf log --category session
sf log --since 2h
sf log --task el-xxxx
sf log --agent el-xxxx
sf log --limit 50
sf log --level error --since 1d
```

## Metrics Command

Show LLM provider usage metrics including token counts, estimated costs, session counts, average duration, and error rates.

```bash
sf metrics [options]
```

| Option                  | Description                                    |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `-r, --range <range>`   | Time range (e.g., 7d, 14d, 30d; default: 7d) |
| `-p, --provider <name>` | Filter by provider name (e.g., claude-code)   |
| `-g, --group-by <mode>` | Group by: provider (default) or model         |

```bash
sf metrics
sf metrics --range 30d
sf metrics --provider claude-code
sf metrics --group-by model
```

## Config Command

Manage Stoneforge configuration. Configuration is loaded from (in order of precedence): CLI flags, environment variables, config file (`.stoneforge/config.yaml`), built-in defaults.

```bash
sf config <subcommand> [args]
```

| Subcommand     | Description                       |
| -------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `show [path]`  | Display current configuration (or a specific key) |
| `set <path> <value>` | Set a configuration value    |
| `unset <path>` | Remove a configuration value      |
| `edit`         | Open config file in editor        |

```bash
sf config show
sf config show actor
sf config show sync.autoExport
sf config set actor myagent
sf config set sync.autoExport true
sf config unset actor
sf config edit
```

## Identity Command

Manage identity settings and view current actor.

```bash
sf identity [subcommand]
```

| Subcommand               | Description                                              |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `whoami`                 | Show current actor identity                              |
| `mode [mode]`            | Show or set identity mode (soft, cryptographic, hybrid)  |
| `sign`                   | Sign data using an Ed25519 private key                   |
| `verify`                 | Verify a signature against data                          |
| `keygen`                 | Generate a new Ed25519 keypair                           |
| `hash`                   | Compute SHA256 hash of data                              |

#### identity sign

| Option                       | Description                              |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-d, --data <string>`        | Data to sign (will be hashed)            |
| `-f, --file <path>`          | File containing data to sign             |
| `--hash <hash>`              | Pre-computed SHA256 hash (hex)           |

Requires `--sign-key` or `--sign-key-file` global flag.

#### identity verify

| Option                       | Description                              |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --signature <sig>`      | Signature to verify (base64, required)   |
| `-k, --public-key <key>`     | Public key (base64, required)            |
| `--signed-at <time>`         | Timestamp when signed (ISO 8601, required) |
| `-d, --data <string>`        | Original data that was signed            |
| `-f, --file <path>`          | File containing original data            |
| `--hash <hash>`              | Request hash that was signed             |

#### identity hash

| Option                       | Description                              |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-d, --data <string>`        | Data to hash                             |
| `-f, --file <path>`          | File to hash                             |

```bash
sf identity
sf identity whoami
sf identity mode
sf identity mode soft
sf identity keygen
sf identity sign --data "hello world" --sign-key <key> --actor alice
sf identity verify --signature <sig> --public-key <key> --signed-at 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z --data "hello" --actor alice
sf identity hash --data "hello world"
```

title: CLI Reference: Data & Communication Commands
content:
# CLI Reference: Data & Communication Commands

Commands for managing entities, documents, plans, workflows, channels, messages, sync, and more.

## Entity Commands

| Command                                    | Description          |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| `sf entity register <name>`                | Register new entity  |
| `sf entity list`                           | List entities        |
| `sf entity set-manager <entity> <manager>` | Set manager          |
| `sf entity clear-manager <entity>`         | Clear manager        |
| `sf entity reports <manager>`              | Get direct reports   |
| `sf entity chain <entity>`                 | Get management chain |

#### entity register

Register a new entity.

| Option                    | Description                                         |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --type <type>`       | Entity type: agent, human, or system (default: agent) |
| `--public-key <key>`      | Base64-encoded Ed25519 public key                   |
| `--tag <tag>`             | Add tag (can be repeated)                           |

```bash
sf entity register alice --type human
sf entity register bot-1 --type agent --tag worker
```

#### entity list

List registered entities.

| Option                | Description                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-t, --type <type>`   | Filter by entity type             |
| `-l, --limit <n>`     | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf entity list --type agent
```

## Document Commands

| Command                               | Description                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `sf document create`                  | Create document                               |
| `sf document list`                    | List documents                                |
| `sf document search <query>`          | Full-text search documents                    |
| `sf document show <id>`               | Show document                                 |
| `sf document update <id>`             | Update document content (creates new version) |
| `sf document history <id>`            | Show version history                          |
| `sf document rollback <id> <version>` | Rollback to version                           |
| `sf document archive <id>`            | Archive document                              |
| `sf document unarchive <id>`          | Unarchive document                            |
| `sf document delete <id>`             | Delete document (soft-delete via tombstone)    |
| `sf document reindex`                 | Reindex documents for FTS5 search             |

#### document create

Create a new document.

| Option                  | Description                                    |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `--title <text>`        | Document title                                 |
| `-c, --content <text>`  | Document content (inline)                      |
| `-f, --file <path>`     | Read content from file                         |
| `-t, --type <type>`     | Document type: text, markdown, or json         |
| `--category <cat>`      | Document category                              |
| `--tag <tag>`           | Add tag (can be repeated)                      |
| `-m, --metadata <json>` | JSON metadata                                  |

#### document list

List documents.

| Option                   | Description                                           |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `-l, --limit <n>`        | Maximum results                                       |
| `-t, --type <type>`      | Filter by document type                               |
| `--category <cat>`       | Filter by category                                    |
| `--status <status>`      | Filter by status: active or archived                  |
| `-a, --all`              | Include archived documents                            |

#### document show

Show document content.

| Option                    | Description                       |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `--doc-version <ver>`     | Show specific version             |

#### document search

Full-text search documents.

| Option                   | Description                       |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `--category <cat>`       | Filter by category                |
| `--status <status>`      | Filter by status                  |
| `-l, --limit <n>`        | Maximum results (default: 50)     |

#### document history

Show version history for a document.

| Option              | Description                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-l, --limit <n>`   | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf document create --title "API Spec" --category spec
sf document list --category spec
sf document search "API authentication"
sf document update el-doc123 --file updated-spec.md
sf document archive abc123
sf document reindex
```

#### document update

Update a document's content, creating a new version. Documents are versioned - each update preserves history.

| Option                    | Description                       |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-c, --content <text>`    | New content (inline)              |
| `-f, --file <path>`       | Read new content from file        |
| `-m, --metadata <json>`   | JSON metadata to merge            |

```bash
sf document update el-doc123 --file path/to/updated.md
```

#### document delete

Delete a document via soft-delete (tombstone). The document's content is preserved but marked as deleted.

| Option                  | Description              |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `-r, --reason <text>`   | Reason for deletion      |
| `-f, --force`           | Skip confirmation        |

```bash
sf document delete el-doc123 --reason "outdated"
```

## Embeddings Commands

| Command                        | Description                    |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| `sf embeddings install`        | Install local embedding model  |
| `sf embeddings status`         | Show embedding model status    |
| `sf embeddings reindex`        | Rebuild document embeddings    |
| `sf embeddings search <query>` | Semantic search over documents |

```bash
sf embeddings install
sf embeddings search "authentication flow"
```

## Plan Commands

| Command                           | Description                       |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `sf plan create`                  | Create plan (defaults to draft)   |
| `sf plan list`                    | List plans                        |
| `sf plan show <id>`               | Show plan details                 |
| `sf plan activate <id>`           | Activate plan (enables dispatch)  |
| `sf plan complete <id>`           | Mark completed                    |
| `sf plan cancel <id>`             | Cancel plan                       |
| `sf plan add-task <id> <task>`    | Add task to plan                  |
| `sf plan remove-task <id> <task>` | Remove task                       |
| `sf plan tasks <id>`              | List tasks in plan                |
| `sf plan auto-complete`           | Auto-complete active plans        |

#### plan create

Create a new plan.

| Option                  | Description                                         |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --title <text>`    | Plan title (required)                               |
| `-s, --status <status>` | Initial status: draft (default) or active           |
| `--tag <tag>`           | Add tag (can be repeated)                           |

```bash
sf plan create --title "Feature X" --tag roadmap
```

#### plan list

List plans.

| Option                  | Description                                         |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --status <status>` | Filter by status: draft, active, completed, cancelled |
| `--tag <tag>`           | Filter by tag (can be repeated for AND logic)       |
| `-l, --limit <n>`       | Maximum results                                     |

```bash
sf plan list --status active
```

#### plan show

Show plan details, optionally including its task list.

| Option           | Description              |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ |
| `-t, --tasks`    | Include task list        |

```bash
sf plan show el-abc123 --tasks
```

#### plan auto-complete

| Option      | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be auto-completed without making changes |

```bash
sf plan auto-complete --dry-run
```

#### plan cancel

Cancel a plan.

| Option                | Description              |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `-r, --reason <text>` | Reason for cancellation  |

```bash
sf plan cancel el-plan123 --reason "Superseded"
```

#### plan tasks

List tasks belonging to a plan.

| Option                  | Description                       |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-s, --status <status>` | Filter by task status             |
| `-l, --limit <n>`       | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf plan tasks el-plan123 --status open
```

### Draft Plan Workflow

Plans default to `draft` status. Tasks in draft plans are NOT dispatchable. Activate a plan after setting up tasks and dependencies to enable dispatch.

## Workflow Commands

| Command                         | Description               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `sf workflow create <playbook>` | Instantiate from playbook |
| `sf workflow list`              | List workflows            |
| `sf workflow show <id>`         | Show details              |
| `sf workflow tasks <id>`        | List tasks                |
| `sf workflow progress <id>`     | Show progress             |
| `sf workflow delete <id>`       | Delete ephemeral          |
| `sf workflow promote <id>`      | Promote to durable        |
| `sf workflow gc`                | Garbage collect           |

#### workflow list

List workflows.

| Option                  | Description                              |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --status <status>` | Filter by status                         |
| `-e, --ephemeral`       | Show only ephemeral workflows            |
| `-d, --durable`         | Show only durable workflows              |
| `-l, --limit <n>`       | Maximum results                          |

```bash
sf workflow list --status running --ephemeral
```

#### workflow tasks

List tasks in a workflow.

| Option                  | Description                       |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-r, --ready`           | Show only ready tasks             |
| `-s, --status <status>` | Filter by task status             |
| `-l, --limit <n>`       | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf workflow tasks el-wf123 --ready
```

#### workflow delete

Delete a workflow.

| Option          | Description                                   |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `-f, --force`   | Required for deleting durable workflows       |

```bash
sf workflow delete el-wf123 --force
```

#### workflow create

| Option                  | Description                               |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `--var <name=value>`    | Set variable (can be repeated)            |
| `-e, --ephemeral`       | Create as ephemeral (not synced to JSONL) |
| `-t, --title <text>`    | Override workflow title                   |

```bash
sf workflow create deploy --var env=prod --ephemeral
```

#### workflow gc

| Option              | Description                                      |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `-a, --age <days>`  | Maximum age in days (default: 7)                 |
| `--dry-run`         | Show what would be deleted without deleting      |

```bash
sf workflow gc --age 14
```

## GC Commands

| Command           | Description                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `sf gc tasks`     | Garbage collect old tasks (deprecated, no-op)  |
| `sf gc workflows` | Garbage collect old ephemeral workflows         |

### sf gc workflows

```bash
sf gc workflows [options]
```

| Option              | Description                              |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-a, --age <days>`  | Maximum age in days (default: 1)         |
| `--dry-run`         | Show what would be deleted               |
| `-l, --limit <n>`   | Maximum number of workflows to delete    |

```bash
sf gc workflows --age 7 --dry-run
```

### sf gc tasks (deprecated)

Task garbage collection is now handled automatically via `sf gc workflows`. This command is kept for backwards compatibility but is effectively a no-op.

## Inbox Commands

| Command                 | Description                          |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `sf inbox <entity>`   | List inbox items with message preview |
| `sf inbox read <id>`    | Mark as read                         |
| `sf inbox read-all <entity>` | Mark all as read for entity     |
| `sf inbox unread <id>`  | Mark as unread                       |
| `sf inbox archive <id>` | Archive item                         |
| `sf inbox count <entity>` | Count unread for entity            |
| `sf show <inbox-id>`    | Show inbox item with full content    |

#### inbox list

List inbox items with message content preview.

| Option                   | Description                                          |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `-a, --all`              | Include read and archived items (default: unread only) |
| `-s, --status <status>`  | Filter by status: unread, read, or archived          |
| `-l, --limit <n>`        | Maximum number of items to return                    |
| `-F, --full`             | Show complete message content instead of truncated   |

```bash
sf inbox alice --full
sf show inbox-abc123
```

## Channel Commands

| Command                           | Description                                             |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sf channel create`               | Create channel (`--description, -D` to set description) |
| `sf channel list`                 | List channels                                           |
| `sf channel join <id>`            | Join channel                                            |
| `sf channel leave <id>`           | Leave channel                                           |
| `sf channel members <id>`         | List members                                            |
| `sf channel add <ch> <entity>`    | Add member                                              |
| `sf channel remove <ch> <entity>` | Remove member                                           |
| `sf channel merge`                | Merge two channels                                      |

#### channel create

| Option                     | Description                                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `-n, --name <name>`        | Channel name (required for group channels)       |
| `-D, --description <text>` | Channel description                              |
| `-t, --type <type>`        | Channel type: group (default) or direct          |
| `--visibility <vis>`           | Visibility: public or private (default)          |
| `-p, --policy <policy>`    | Join policy: open, invite-only (default), or request |
| `-m, --member <id>`        | Add member (can be repeated)                     |
| `-d, --direct <entity>`    | Create direct channel with entity (for --type direct) |
| `--tag <tag>`              | Add tag (can be repeated)                        |

```bash
sf channel create --name general --description "General discussion"
sf channel create --type direct --direct el-user123
```

#### channel list

List channels.

| Option                | Description                              |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --type <type>`   | Filter by type: group or direct          |
| `-m, --member <id>`   | Filter by member                         |
| `-l, --limit <n>`     | Maximum results                          |

```bash
sf channel list --type group --member alice
```

#### channel merge

| Option                  | Description                              |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --source <id>`     | Source channel ID (required)             |
| `-t, --target <id>`     | Target channel ID (required)             |
| `-n, --name <new-name>` | Optional new name for the merged channel |

```bash
sf channel merge -s el-ch111 -t el-ch222 --name "combined-channel"
```

## Message Commands

| Command                  | Description                                        |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `sf message send`        | Send message to channel, entity, or as reply       |
| `sf message reply <id>`  | Reply to a message (shorthand for send --reply-to) |
| `sf message thread <id>` | View thread messages                               |
| `sf message list`        | List messages                                      |

#### message send

| Option                  | Description                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-c, --channel <id>`    | Channel to send to                                                               |
| `-T, --to <entity>`     | Entity to send DM to (finds or creates DM channel)                               |
| `-r, --reply-to <msg>`  | Message ID to reply to (auto-sets channel, thread, swaps sender/recipient in DM) |
| `-m, --content <text>`  | Message content                                                                  |
| `--file <path>`         | Read content from file                                                           |
| `-t, --thread <id>`     | Reply to message (creates thread)                                                |
| `-a, --attachment <id>` | Attach document (can be repeated)                                                |
| `--tag <tag>`           | Add tag (can be repeated)                                                        |

```bash
sf message send --channel el-abc123 --content "Hello!"
sf message send --to el-user456 -m "Direct message"
sf message send --reply-to el-msg789 -m "Reply"
```

#### message reply

| Option                  | Description                       |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-m, --content <text>`  | Message content                   |
| `--file <path>`         | Read content from file            |
| `-a, --attachment <id>` | Attach document (can be repeated) |
| `--tag <tag>`           | Add tag (can be repeated)         |

```bash
sf message reply el-msg123 --content "Thanks for the update!"
sf --from bot message reply el-msg123 -m "Automated response"
```

#### message list

| Option                 | Description                              |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `-c, --channel <id>`   | Channel ID (required)                    |
| `-s, --sender <id>`    | Filter by sender                         |
| `-r, --root-only`      | Show only root messages (no replies)     |
| `-l, --limit <n>`      | Maximum results                          |

```bash
sf message list --channel el-ch123 --sender alice
```

#### message thread

View thread messages for a message.

| Option              | Description                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-l, --limit <n>`   | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf message thread el-msg123
sf message thread el-msg123 --limit 50
```

## Team Commands

| Command                          | Description   |
| -------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `sf team create`                 | Create team   |
| `sf team list`                   | List teams    |
| `sf team add <team> <entity>`    | Add member    |
| `sf team remove <team> <entity>` | Remove member |
| `sf team members <id>`           | List members  |
| `sf team delete <id>`            | Delete team   |

#### team create

Create a new team.

| Option                | Description                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-n, --name <name>`   | Team name (required)              |
| `-m, --member <id>`   | Add member (can be repeated)      |
| `--tag <tag>`         | Add tag (can be repeated)         |

```bash
sf team create --name "Backend Team" --member alice
```

#### team list

List teams.

| Option                | Description                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-m, --member <id>`   | Filter by member                  |
| `-l, --limit <n>`     | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf team list --member alice
```

#### team delete

Delete a team.

| Option                | Description              |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `-r, --reason <text>` | Reason for deletion      |
| `-f, --force`         | Skip confirmation for teams with members |

```bash
sf team delete el-team123 --force
```

## Library Commands

| Command                              | Description                      |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `sf library create`                  | Create a new library             |
| `sf library list`                    | List libraries                   |
| `sf library roots`                   | List root libraries              |
| `sf library docs <id>`              | List documents in a library      |
| `sf library stats <id>`             | Show library statistics          |
| `sf library add <lib> <doc>`        | Add document to library          |
| `sf library remove <lib> <doc>`     | Remove document from library     |
| `sf library nest <child> <parent>`  | Nest a library under another     |
| `sf library delete <id>`            | Delete a library                 |

#### library create

Create a new library.

| Option                | Description                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-n, --name <name>`   | Library name (required)           |
| `--tag <tag>`         | Add tag (can be repeated)         |

#### library list

List libraries.

| Option              | Description                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-l, --limit <n>`   | Maximum results                   |

#### library delete

Delete a library. By default, deletion is prevented if the library has contents.

| Option              | Description                                         |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-f, --force`       | Force deletion even if library has contents         |

```bash
sf library delete el-lib123
sf library delete el-lib123 --force
```

## Doctor Command

Check system health and diagnose issues.

```bash
sf doctor [options]
```

| Option       | Description                                           |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--fix`      | Automatically repair detected issues (FK violations, blocked cache) |

**Checks performed:**

Database health:
- Workspace exists (`.stoneforge` directory)
- Database file exists and can be opened
- Schema version is current
- All expected tables are present
- Database integrity check (`PRAGMA integrity_check`)
- Foreign key constraint validation
- Blocked cache consistency
- Storage statistics

Runtime health (via smithy-server, skipped if unavailable):
- Rate limit status: which executables are limited, when they reset
- Stuck tasks: tasks with high resumeCount and no active session
- Merge queue health: tasks stuck in testing/merging
- Error rate: recent errors from operation log
- Agent pool: utilization and active sessions

**Auto-repair (`--fix`):**
- Deletes orphaned rows that violate foreign key constraints
- Rebuilds the blocked cache from the dependency graph

```bash
sf doctor
sf doctor --verbose
sf doctor --fix
sf doctor --json
```

## Migrate Command

Run database migrations to update the schema.

```bash
sf migrate [options]
```

| Option       | Description                                           |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--dry-run`  | Show what migrations would be applied without running them |

Migrations are run automatically when needed, but this command can be used to manually trigger migration or check pending migrations.

```bash
sf migrate
sf migrate --dry-run
```

## Sync Commands

| Command           | Description                       |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `sf sync export`  | Export elements to JSONL files    |
| `sf sync import`  | Import elements from JSONL files  |
| `sf sync status`  | Show sync status                  |

Top-level commands `sf export`, `sf import`, and `sf status` are also available as shortcuts.

#### sync export

Export elements and dependencies to JSONL files for version control. By default, only exports elements modified since the last export (incremental).

```bash
sf sync export [options]
```

| Option                  | Description                                   |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `-o, --output <dir>`    | Output directory (default: `.stoneforge/sync`) |
| `-f, --full`            | Full export (ignore dirty tracking)           |
| `--include-ephemeral`   | Include ephemeral elements (excluded by default) |

```bash
sf export
sf export --full
sf export -o ./backup
```

#### sync import

Import elements and dependencies from JSONL files. Uses Last-Write-Wins (LWW) merge strategy by default.

```bash
sf sync import [options]
```

| Option                | Description                                    |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `-i, --input <dir>`   | Input directory (default: `.stoneforge/sync`)  |
| `-n, --dry-run`       | Show what would change without importing       |
| `-f, --force`         | Force import (remote always wins)              |

```bash
sf import
sf import --dry-run
sf import --force
```

#### sync status

Show the current sync status (dirty element count, sync directory status).

```bash
sf sync status
sf status
```

## External Sync Commands

Manage bidirectional sync with external services (GitHub, Linear, folder-based providers).

| Command                              | Description                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `sf external-sync config`            | Show provider configuration                          |
| `sf external-sync config set-token`  | Set authentication token for a provider              |
| `sf external-sync config set-project`| Set default project for a provider                   |
| `sf external-sync config set-auto-link` | Enable auto-linking for a provider                |
| `sf external-sync config disable-auto-link` | Disable auto-linking                           |
| `sf external-sync link`              | Link a task or document to an external issue/page    |
| `sf external-sync link-all`          | Bulk-link all unlinked tasks or documents            |
| `sf external-sync unlink`            | Remove external link from a task or document         |
| `sf external-sync unlink-all`        | Bulk-remove external links from all linked elements  |
| `sf external-sync push`              | Push linked elements to external service             |
| `sf external-sync pull`              | Pull changes from external for linked elements       |
| `sf external-sync sync`              | Bidirectional sync (push + pull)                     |
| `sf external-sync status`            | Show external sync state overview                    |
| `sf external-sync resolve`           | Resolve a sync conflict                              |

#### external-sync config

Show current external sync configuration including enabled providers, conflict strategy, and auto-link settings.

```bash
sf external-sync config
```

#### external-sync config set-token

```bash
sf external-sync config set-token <provider> <token>
```

```bash
sf external-sync config set-token github ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxx
sf external-sync config set-token linear lin_api_xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

#### external-sync config set-project

```bash
sf external-sync config set-project <provider> <project>
```

```bash
sf external-sync config set-project github owner/repo
sf external-sync config set-project linear PROJECT-KEY
```

#### external-sync config set-auto-link

Enable auto-linking new elements to the specified provider.

```bash
sf external-sync config set-auto-link <provider> [options]
```

| Option                | Description                                          |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --type <type>`   | Element type: `task` or `document` (default: `task`) |

```bash
sf external-sync config set-auto-link github
sf external-sync config set-auto-link folder --type document
```

#### external-sync config disable-auto-link

```bash
sf external-sync config disable-auto-link [options]
```

| Option                | Description                                                    |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-t, --type <type>`   | Element type: `task`, `document`, or `all` (default: `all`)    |

#### external-sync link

Link a task or document to an external issue or page.

```bash
sf external-sync link <elementId> <url-or-external-id> [options]
```

| Option                  | Description                                    |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `-p, --provider <name>` | Provider name (default: `github`)              |
| `-t, --type <type>`     | Element type: `task` or `document` (default: `task`) |

```bash
sf external-sync link el-abc123 https://github.com/org/repo/issues/42
sf external-sync link el-doc456 https://linear.app/team/DOC-1 --provider linear --type document
```

#### external-sync link-all

Bulk-link all unlinked tasks or documents to a provider. Creates external issues/pages for each unlinked element.

```bash
sf external-sync link-all [options]
```

| Option                    | Description                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-p, --provider <name>`   | Provider to link to (required)                                  |
| `--project <project>`     | Override the default project                                    |
| `-s, --status <status>`   | Only link elements with this status (repeatable)                |
| `-n, --dry-run`            | List elements that would be linked without creating issues      |
| `-b, --batch-size <n>`    | Elements to process concurrently (default: 10)                  |
| `-f, --force`              | Re-link elements already linked (including same provider)       |
| `-t, --type <type>`       | Element type: `task` or `document` (default: `task`)            |
| `--no-library`             | Include documents not in any library (excluded by default)      |

```bash
sf external-sync link-all --provider github --dry-run
sf external-sync link-all --provider github --status open --status in_progress
sf external-sync link-all --provider folder --type document
```

#### external-sync unlink

Remove the external link from a task or document.

```bash
sf external-sync unlink <elementId>
```

#### external-sync unlink-all

Bulk-remove external links from all linked elements.

```bash
sf external-sync unlink-all [options]
```

| Option                  | Description                                               |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-p, --provider <name>` | Only unlink elements linked to this provider             |
| `-t, --type <type>`     | Element type: `task`, `document`, or `all` (default: `all`) |
| `-n, --dry-run`          | Show what would be unlinked without making changes       |

```bash
sf external-sync unlink-all --provider github --dry-run
sf external-sync unlink-all --type task
```

#### external-sync push

Push linked elements to their external service. Only pushes elements that have changed since the last sync.

```bash
sf external-sync push [elementId...] [options]
```

| Option                | Description                                                    |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-a, --all`           | Push all linked elements                                       |
| `-f, --force`         | Push all regardless of changes                                 |
| `-t, --type <type>`   | Element type: `task`, `document`, or `all` (default: `all`)    |
| `--no-library`         | Include documents not in any library (excluded by default)    |

```bash
sf external-sync push el-abc123
sf external-sync push --all
sf external-sync push --all --force --type task
```

#### external-sync pull

Pull changes from external services for linked elements.

```bash
sf external-sync pull [options]
```

| Option                  | Description                                               |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-p, --provider <name>` | Provider to pull from (default: all configured)          |
| `-d, --discover`        | Discover new external issues not yet linked              |
| `-t, --type <type>`     | Element type: `task`, `document`, or `all` (default: `all`) |

```bash
sf external-sync pull
sf external-sync pull --provider github --discover
sf external-sync pull --type document
```

#### external-sync sync

Bidirectional sync — pushes local changes and pulls remote changes.

```bash
sf external-sync sync [options]
```

| Option                | Description                                                    |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-n, --dry-run`       | Show what would change without making changes                  |
| `-t, --type <type>`   | Element type: `task`, `document`, or `all` (default: `all`)    |

```bash
sf external-sync sync
sf external-sync sync --dry-run
sf external-sync sync --type task
```

#### external-sync status

Show external sync state overview including linked elements and their sync status.

```bash
sf external-sync status
```

#### external-sync resolve

Resolve a sync conflict for a linked element.

```bash
sf external-sync resolve <elementId> [options]
```

| Option                | Description                                    |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `-k, --keep <version>`| Which version to keep: `local` or `remote` (required) |

```bash
sf external-sync resolve el-abc123 --keep local
sf external-sync resolve el-abc123 --keep remote
```

## Docs Commands

Documentation infrastructure commands.

#### docs init

## Playbook Commands

Manage playbooks (workflow templates).

| Command                            | Description                              |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `sf playbook list`                 | List playbooks                           |
| `sf playbook show <name\|id>`      | Show playbook details                    |
| `sf playbook validate <name\|id>`  | Validate playbook structure              |
| `sf playbook create`               | Create a new playbook                    |

#### playbook list

| Option              | Description                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-l, --limit <n>`   | Maximum results                   |

```bash
sf playbook list
```

#### playbook show

| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `-s, --steps`       | Include step definitions          |
| `--variables`       | Include variable definitions      |


#### playbook validate

Validate a playbook's structure and optionally test create-time variable resolution.

| Option                  | Description                                           |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--var <name=value>`    | Set variable for create-time validation (repeatable)  |
| `-c, --create`          | Perform create-time validation                        |

#### playbook create

| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-n, --name <name>`     | Playbook name (unique identifier, required)         |
| `-t, --title <title>`   | Playbook title (display name, required)             |
| `-s, --step <spec>`     | Add step: `id:title[:dep1,dep2]` (repeatable)       |
| `--variable <spec>`     | Add variable: `name:type[:default][:required]` (repeatable) |
