title: CLI Reference: Agent & Orchestration Commands
content:
# CLI Reference: Agent & Orchestration Commands

Commands for managing agents, the dispatch daemon, task dispatching, merge operations, and agent pools.

## Merge Command

Squash-merge a branch into the default branch (master/main). This command fetches latest from origin, creates a temporary worktree at the target branch, squash-merges the source branch into it, commits and pushes to origin, then cleans up the temporary worktree. Optionally removes the source branch and worktree with `--cleanup`.

| Option                  | Description                                         |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-b, --branch <name>`   | Source branch to merge (default: current branch)    |
| `-i, --into <name>`     | Target branch (default: master/main auto-detected)  |
| `-m, --message <text>`  | Commit message (default: "Merge \<branch\>")        |
| `--cleanup`             | Delete source branch and worktree after merge       |

```bash
sf merge
sf merge --message "feat: implement user auth"
sf merge --branch feature/xyz --into main
sf merge --cleanup --message "docs: automated documentation fixes"
```

## Agent Commands

Manage orchestrator agents (registration, lifecycle, streaming).

| Command                          | Description                          |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `sf agent list`                  | List all registered agents           |
| `sf agent show <id>`             | Show agent details                   |
| `sf agent register <name>`       | Register a new agent                 |
| `sf agent start <id>`            | Start an agent process               |
| `sf agent stop <id>`             | Stop an agent session                |
| `sf agent stream <id>`           | Get agent channel for streaming      |

#### agent list

| Option                       | Description                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `-r, --role <role>`          | Filter by role (director, worker, steward)            |
| `-s, --status <status>`      | Filter by session status (idle, running, suspended, terminated) |
| `-m, --workerMode <mode>`    | Filter by worker mode (ephemeral, persistent)         |
| `-f, --focus <focus>`        | Filter by steward focus (merge, docs, recovery, custom) |
| `--reportsTo <id>`           | Filter by manager entity ID                           |
| `--hasSession`               | Filter to agents with active sessions                 |

```bash
sf agent list
sf agent list --role worker
sf agent list --role worker --workerMode ephemeral
sf agent list --status running
sf agent list --role steward --focus merge
```

#### agent show

```bash
sf agent show el-abc123
```

No additional options beyond global flags.

#### agent register

| Option                       | Description                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `-r, --role <role>`          | Agent role: director, worker, steward (required)      |
| `-m, --mode <mode>`          | Worker mode: ephemeral, persistent (default: ephemeral) |
| `-f, --focus <focus>`        | Steward focus: merge, docs, recovery, custom          |
| `-t, --maxTasks <n>`         | Maximum concurrent tasks (default: 1)                 |
| `--tags <tags>`              | Comma-separated tags                                  |
| `--reportsTo <id>`           | Manager entity ID (for workers/stewards)              |
| `--roleDef <id>`             | Role definition document ID                           |
| `--trigger <cron>`           | Steward cron trigger (e.g., `"0 2 * * *"`)           |
| `--provider <name>`          | Agent provider (e.g., claude-code, opencode)          |
| `--model <model>`            | LLM model to use (e.g., claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929)  |
| `--target-branch <branch>`   | Target branch for merge (director only, default: auto-detect) |

```bash
sf agent register MyWorker --role worker --mode ephemeral
sf agent register MainDirector --role director
sf agent register MergeSteward --role steward --focus merge
sf agent register DocsSteward --role steward --focus docs --trigger "0 9 * * *"
sf agent register OcWorker --role worker --provider opencode
```

#### agent start

| Option                       | Description                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `-p, --prompt <text>`        | Initial prompt to send to the agent                   |
| `-m, --mode <mode>`          | Start mode: headless, interactive                     |
| `-r, --resume <id>`          | Resume a previous session                             |
| `-w, --workdir <path>`       | Working directory for the agent                       |
| `--cols <n>`                 | Terminal columns for interactive mode (default: 120)  |
| `--rows <n>`                 | Terminal rows for interactive mode (default: 30)      |
| `--timeout <ms>`             | Timeout in milliseconds (default: 120000)             |
| `-e, --env <KEY=VALUE>`      | Environment variable to set (repeatable)              |
| `-t, --taskId <id>`          | Task ID to assign to this agent                       |
| `--stream`                   | Stream agent output after starting                    |
| `--provider <name>`          | Override agent provider for this session              |
| `--model <model>`            | Override model for this session                       |

```bash
sf agent start el-abc123
sf agent start el-abc123 --mode interactive
sf agent start el-abc123 --prompt "Start working on your assigned tasks"
sf agent start el-abc123 --resume prev-session-id
sf agent start el-abc123 --taskId el-task456 --stream
```

#### agent stop

| Option                       | Description                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `-g, --graceful`             | Graceful shutdown (default: true)                     |
| `--no-graceful`              | Force immediate shutdown                              |
| `-r, --reason <text>`        | Reason for stopping the agent                         |

```bash
sf agent stop el-abc123
sf agent stop el-abc123 --reason "Task completed"
sf agent stop el-abc123 --no-graceful
```

#### agent stream

```bash
sf agent stream el-abc123
```

No additional options beyond global flags.

## Daemon Commands

Manage the dispatch daemon (automatic task assignment to agents).

| Command                | Description                                      |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `sf daemon start`      | Start the dispatch daemon                        |
| `sf daemon stop`       | Stop the dispatch daemon                         |
| `sf daemon status`     | Show daemon status (including rate limit info)   |
| `sf daemon sleep`      | Pause dispatch until a specified time            |
| `sf daemon wake`       | Immediately resume dispatch                      |

All daemon subcommands accept `-s, --server <url>` to specify the orchestrator server URL (default: `http://localhost:3457`).

#### daemon start

```bash
sf daemon start
sf daemon start --server http://localhost:8080
```

#### daemon stop

| Option                    | Description                                                |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --server <url>`      | Orchestrator server URL (default: `http://localhost:3457`) |
| `-f, --force`             | Skip confirmation prompt                                   |

```bash
sf daemon stop
sf daemon stop --force
```

#### daemon status

Displays whether the daemon is running, dispatch statistics, and rate limit/sleep status.

```bash
sf daemon status
sf daemon status --json
```

#### daemon sleep

Manually puts the daemon into a rate-limit sleep state, pausing all task dispatch until the specified time. Non-dispatch polls (inbox, plan auto-complete, etc.) continue running.

| Option                    | Description                                |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `-s, --server <url>`      | Orchestrator server URL (default: `http://localhost:3457`) |
| `-u, --until <time>`      | Sleep until a specific time (e.g., `"3am"`, `"Feb 22 at 9:30am"`, `"tomorrow at 3pm"`) |
| `-d, --duration <secs>`   | Sleep for a duration in seconds            |

```bash
sf daemon sleep --until "3am"
sf daemon sleep --until "tomorrow at 3pm"
sf daemon sleep --duration 3600
```

#### daemon wake

Clears all rate limit entries and the sleep timer, resuming normal dispatch on the next poll cycle.

```bash
sf daemon wake
```

## Dispatch Command

Dispatch a task to an agent for execution.

```bash
sf dispatch <task-id> <agent-id> [options]
```

| Option                       | Description                               |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `-b, --branch <branch>`      | Git branch for the task                   |
| `-w, --worktree <path>`      | Worktree path for the task                |
| `-s, --session <id>`         | Session ID to associate                   |
| `-m, --markAsStarted`        | Mark the task as started after dispatch   |

```bash
sf dispatch el-abc123 el-agent1
sf dispatch el-abc123 el-agent1 --branch feature/my-task
sf dispatch el-abc123 el-agent1 --markAsStarted
```

## Pool Commands

Manage agent pools for concurrency limiting. Agent pools limit the maximum number of agents running concurrently; when a pool is at capacity, new agent spawns are blocked until slots become available.

| Command                       | Description                           |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `sf pool list`                | List all agent pools                  |
| `sf pool show <id\|name>`     | Show pool details                     |
| `sf pool create <name>`       | Create a new pool                     |
| `sf pool update <id\|name>`   | Update pool configuration             |
| `sf pool delete <id\|name>`   | Delete a pool                         |
| `sf pool status <id\|name>`   | Show pool status with active agents   |
| `sf pool refresh`             | Refresh pool status from sessions     |

#### pool create

| Option                       | Description                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --size <n>`             | Maximum pool size (default: 5)                        |
| `-d, --description <text>`   | Pool description                                      |
| `-t, --agentType <config>`   | Agent type config (repeatable). Format: `role[:mode\|focus][:priority][:maxSlots][:provider][:model]` |
| `--tags <tags>`              | Comma-separated tags                                  |
| `--disabled`                 | Create pool in disabled state                         |

```bash
sf pool create default --size 5
sf pool create workers --size 10 -t worker:ephemeral -t worker:persistent
sf pool create merge-pool --size 2 -t steward:merge:100
sf pool create ai-pool --size 3 -t worker:ephemeral:100:5:claude-code:claude-sonnet-4-20250514
```

#### pool update

| Option                       | Description                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `-s, --size <n>`             | Maximum pool size                                     |
| `-d, --description <text>`   | Pool description                                      |
| `-t, --agentType <config>`   | Agent type config (replaces existing, repeatable)     |
| `--tags <tags>`              | Comma-separated tags (replaces existing)              |
| `--enable`                   | Enable the pool                                       |
| `--disable`                  | Disable the pool                                      |

```bash
sf pool update default --size 10
sf pool update workers --enable
sf pool update merge-pool --disable
```

#### pool show

```bash
sf pool show default
```

No additional options beyond global flags.

#### pool status

```bash
sf pool status default
```

No additional options beyond global flags.

#### pool delete

| Option           | Description                        |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `-f, --force`    | Delete even if agents are active   |

```bash
sf pool delete old-pool
sf pool delete el-abc123 --force
```

#### pool refresh

Refresh the status of all agent pools based on current sessions.

```bash
sf pool refresh
```
Task assigned: Fix findSkillsSourceDir to resolve skills via module resolution for all package managers [Priority: 1]

## Goal

Extend the onboarding tour infrastructure to support cross-page navigation, sectioned progress, and skip-section functionality. This is the foundation that Task 2 builds on.

## Files to Modify

1. **`apps/smithy-web/src/components/onboarding/OnboardingTour.tsx`**
2. **`apps/smithy-web/src/hooks/useOnboardingTour.ts`**

## Requirements

### TourStep Interface Extension (OnboardingTour.tsx, line 24-35)

Add three optional fields to the existing `TourStep` interface:

```ts
export interface TourStep {
  id: string;
  targetTestId: string;
  title: string;
  description: string;
  enabled?: boolean;
  // NEW:
  route?: string;           // Page this step targets (e.g., '/tasks')
  section?: string;          // Group label for progress bar (e.g., 'Tasks & Plans')
  onActivate?: () => void;   // Side effect before showing step (expand sidebar, etc.)
}
```

### Sectioned Progress Bar (OnboardingTour.tsx, lines 329-345)

Replace the individual dots with a segmented progress bar:

- Each segment represents a `section` (group of steps sharing the same `section` string)
- Current section segment partially fills based on progress within that section
- Completed sections are fully filled, future sections are empty
- Below the bar: show section label + "Step N of M" text
- The `TourTooltip` component needs to accept the full `steps: TourStep[]` array instead of just `totalSteps: number`

### isNavigating Prop (OnboardingTour.tsx)

Add `isNavigating?: boolean` to `OnboardingTourProps`. When `isNavigating && !targetRect`:
- Render the backdrop overlay WITHOUT spotlight (prevents flash of nothing between pages)
- Optionally show a small centered loading indicator

### Extended Polling (OnboardingTour.tsx, lines 424-425)

- Current: polls every 500ms for 3 seconds
- New: if `currentStepData.route` exists, poll for 5 seconds instead (route component needs time to mount)

### Auto-Advance on Missing Target

If target element is not found after the full polling duration, automatically advance to the next step. This prevents users from getting stuck on steps where the target conditionally doesn't render.

### Skip Section Link

Add a "Skip section" text link in the tooltip footer (left side, next to Back), styled as subtle/tertiary. It calls `onSkipSection()` which is a new prop on `OnboardingTourProps`.

### useOnboardingTour Hook Changes (useOnboardingTour.ts)

**Change signature** from `useOnboardingTour(totalSteps: number)` to `useOnboardingTour(steps: TourStep[])`:
- Internally compute `activeSteps` (filter `enabled !== false`)
- Compute `totalSteps` from `activeSteps.length`
- Compute sections from `step.section` grouping

**Add functions:**
- `goToStep(index: number)` - set currentStep to arbitrary index
- `skipSection()` - jump to first step of the next section (using the internal sections computation)

**Add `currentSection` and `totalSections`** to the returned state.

**Persist currentStep** to localStorage (key: `stoneforge:onboarding-step`):
- On mount, if tour is not completed, restore currentStep
- Clear on `markCompleted()` and `reset()`

## Workspace Documentation

Before starting, search workspace docs: `sf document search "onboarding"` and `sf document search "tour"`. Update any relevant docs. If you create new docs, add them to the library with `sf docs add <doc-id>`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- TourStep interface has `route`, `section`, `onActivate` fields
- Progress bar renders sections instead of dots
- isNavigating prop shows overlay during page transitions
- Polling extends to 5s for steps with route field
- Auto-advance works when target not found
- Skip section link appears and works
- Hook accepts TourStep[] and computes sections
- currentStep persists across browser refresh
- All existing functionality (keyboard nav, conditional steps, restart from settings) still works

## Goal

Define the full 28-step tutorial with 7 sections covering every major feature area, and wire up cross-page navigation in AppShell.

## Depends On

Task "Onboarding tour: core infrastructure" must be completed first (provides the extended TourStep interface, section support, isNavigating prop, etc.).

## Files to Modify

1. **`apps/smithy-web/src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx`** (primary)
2. **`apps/smithy-web/src/routes/plans/index.tsx`** (add missing data-testid)

## Requirements

### Replace ONBOARDING_STEPS (AppShell.tsx, lines 311-356)

Replace the current 6-step array with 28 steps across 7 sections. Each step declares its `section`, `route` (if cross-page), and `onActivate` (if side effects needed).

#### Section 1: "Command Center" (route: /activity) -- 4 steps
| id | targetTestId | title | description |
|----|-------------|-------|-------------|
| welcome | activity-page | Welcome to Stoneforge | Your command center -- see all active agents, tasks, and system health at a glance. |
| system-status | system-status-bar | System Status | These indicators show active agents, in-progress tasks, and merge request pipeline health. A quick pulse check. |
| agent-cards | active-agents-section | Active Agents | Each card is a running agent showing its status, current task, and live output. Click one to open its terminal. |
| header-bar | header | Global Controls | The header gives you the command palette (Cmd+K), daemon toggle, emergency stop, notifications, and theme switch -- available on every page. |

#### Section 2: "Managing Work" (routes: /tasks, /plans, /merge-requests) -- 5 steps
| id | route | targetTestId | title | description |
|----|-------|-------------|-------|-------------|
| tasks-overview | /tasks | tasks-page | Task Board | All work items live here. Switch between list and Kanban views, filter by status tabs, search, sort, and group tasks however you like. |
| tasks-create | /tasks | tasks-create | Create Tasks | Click here to create new tasks. Assign them to agents, set priorities, and attach them to plans. |
| tasks-views | /tasks | tasks-tab-in-progress | Status Tabs | Filter tasks by lifecycle stage. "In Progress" and "Awaiting Merge" show what agents are actively working on. |
| plans-overview | /plans | plans-page | Plans & Roadmap | Plans group related tasks into a coordinated effort. Switch to Roadmap view for a timeline visualization. |
| merge-requests | /merge-requests | merge-requests-page | Merge Requests | When agents complete work, their branches appear here. Review diffs, approve, request changes, or merge directly. |

#### Section 3: "Agent Fleet" (routes: /agents, /workspaces) -- 4 steps
| id | route | targetTestId | title | description |
|----|-------|-------------|-------|-------------|
| agents-overview | /agents | agents-page | Agent Registry | Meet your fleet: Directors orchestrate, Workers execute tasks, Stewards review code. Create, configure, and manage agents here. |
| agents-create | /agents | agents-create | Create Agents | Add new agents to expand your team. Each worker gets its own git worktree and can be assigned tasks independently. |

## Goal

Replace the current text-input prompt for workflow preset selection in \`sf init\` with an interactive arrow-key selector (up/down + enter).

## Current Behavior

**File:** \`packages/quarry/src/cli/commands/init.ts\`, function \`promptWorkflowPreset()\` (lines 415-448)

Currently uses Node.js \`readline\` to show a text menu and asks the user to type the preset name:

\`\`\`
? Choose a workflow preset:
  ❯ Auto      — Agents merge directly to main. Fast iteration, no human review.
    Review    — Agents merge to a review branch. You review and merge to main.
    Approve   — Agents need approval for restricted actions. Merges via GitHub PRs.

Enter preset (auto/review/approve) [auto]:
\`\`\`

The user must type "auto", "review", or "approve". This is clunky -- users expect arrow-key navigation.

## Desired Behavior

An interactive selector where:
- The 3 options are displayed with descriptions
- User navigates with up/down arrow keys
- Current selection is highlighted (e.g., with \`❯\` marker and/or color)
- Enter key confirms the selection
- Default selection is "auto" (first item)

Example visual:

\`\`\`
? Choose a workflow preset:
  ❯ Auto      — Agents merge directly to main. Fast iteration, no human review.
    Review    — Agents merge to a review branch. You review and merge to main.
    Approve   — Agents need approval for restricted actions. Merges via GitHub PRs.
\`\`\`

Arrow down moves the \`❯\` indicator. Enter confirms.

## Implementation Approach

**Do NOT add external dependencies** (no inquirer, prompts, etc.). Implement using Node.js built-in \`readline\` with raw mode for keypress handling. This matches the project's existing pattern of using only built-in Node.js modules for CLI interaction.

The approach:
1. Put stdin in raw mode (\`process.stdin.setRawMode(true)\`)
2. Listen for keypress events (data events on stdin)
3. Parse arrow key escape sequences: \`\\x1B[A\` (up), \`\\x1B[B\` (down)
4. Parse enter key: \`\\r\` or \`\\n\`
5. Parse Ctrl+C: \`\\x03\` (exit gracefully)
6. On each keypress, clear the menu lines and redraw with updated selection
7. Use ANSI escape codes for cursor movement and line clearing

Key ANSI codes needed:
- \`\\x1B[F\` — move cursor up one line
- \`\\x1B[2K\` — clear entire line
- \`\\x1B[?25l\` — hide cursor
- \`\\x1B[?25h\` — show cursor

The presets, their labels, and descriptions are already defined:
- \`VALID_WORKFLOW_PRESETS\`: \`['auto', 'review', 'approve']\`
- \`PRESET_DESCRIPTIONS\`: descriptions for each preset

## Architecture of the Logging

The output comes from multiple sources:

| Source | Logging mechanism | Files |
|--------|------------------|-------|
| \`[orchestrator]\` | \`createLogger('orchestrator')\` from \`packages/smithy/src/utils/logger.ts\` | \`packages/smithy/src/server/index.ts\`, \`packages/smithy/src/server/server.ts\` |
| \`[lsp-manager]\` | \`createLogger('lsp-manager')\` | \`packages/smithy/src/server/services/lsp-manager.ts\` |
| \`[static]\` | \`createLogger('static')\` | \`packages/smithy/src/server/static.ts\` |
| \`[ws]\` | Direct \`console.log\` | \`packages/shared-routes/src/ws/broadcaster.ts\` |
| \`[auto-export]\` | Direct \`console.log\` | \`packages/quarry/src/sync/auto-export.ts\` |

The final "Smithy server running at" line comes from \`packages/quarry/src/cli/commands/serve.ts\` line 109.

## Implementation Approach

**Strategy**: Rather than silencing all the subsystem loggers (which would lose useful debug info), set the default log level to WARNING during startup, capture the key info, then print a clean summary.

### Option A (Recommended): Startup summary in serve.ts

1. **In \`serve.ts\`**: After \`startSmithyServer()\` returns, print the branded summary using the returned port and collected info
2. **Set \`LOG_LEVEL=WARNING\` before startup** (only if not explicitly set by user): This suppresses all INFO-level startup messages from the logger-based subsystems
3. **Redirect \`console.log\` during startup** to capture/suppress the direct \`console.log\` lines from \`[ws]\` and \`[auto-export]\`
4. **After startup completes**: Restore \`console.log\` and print the clean summary

The console.log interception pattern:
\`\`\`typescript
const originalLog = console.log;
const startupLogs: string[] = [];
console.log = (...args: unknown[]) => {
  const msg = args.map(String).join(' ');
  startupLogs.push(msg); // capture for debug if needed
};

// ... start server ...

console.log = originalLog; // restore

// Parse startupLogs for useful info (agent count, daemon status, etc.)
// Print clean summary
\`\`\`

### Option B: Add a quiet/startup mode to the logger

Add a \`logger.setStartupMode(true)\` that suppresses output, then \`logger.setStartupMode(false)\` after startup. This is cleaner but requires changes to the logger utility.

**Recommendation**: Option A is simpler and self-contained in serve.ts. The captured logs can still be written to a log file or shown with a \`--verbose\` flag.

## Goal

## Approach: React Query Cache Injection

All data in the smithy-web app flows through React Query hooks (useAgents, useTasks, usePlans, etc.). By calling \`queryClient.setQueryData()\` we can inject mock data that immediately appears in every component using those hooks — zero component changes needed.

## File to Create

\`apps/smithy-web/src/components/onboarding/tourMockData.ts\`

## API

\`\`\`typescript
import type { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';

/** Inject mock data for a specific tour context into the React Query cache */
export function injectTourMockData(
  queryClient: QueryClient,
  context: 'activity' | 'tasks' | 'plans' | 'documents' | 'messages'
): void;

/** Clear all tour mock data from the React Query cache and refetch real data */
export function clearTourMockData(queryClient: QueryClient): void;

/** Check if tour mock data is currently injected */
export function hasTourMockData(): boolean;
\`\`\`

### Tasks context (mock tasks for the task board)

## Implementation Details

### Mock ID Convention

Use a consistent prefix for all mock IDs: \`tour-mock-\` (e.g., \`tour-mock-task-1\`, \`tour-mock-agent-director\`). This makes cleanup easy and prevents collision with real data.

### State Tracking

Use a module-level variable to track which context is currently injected:
\`\`\`typescript
let currentContext: string | null = null;
\`\`\`

### Cleanup

\`clearTourMockData\` should:
1. Invalidate all query keys that were set with mock data
2. Reset \`currentContext\` to null
3. Call \`queryClient.refetchQueries()\` on the affected keys to restore real data

- \`useAgents()\` in \`apps/smithy-web/src/api/hooks/useAgents.ts\` → find \`queryKey\`
- \`useTasks()\` or \`useTasksByStatus()\` → find query keys
- \`usePlans()\` → find query keys
- \`useDocuments()\` or \`useLibraries()\` → find query keys
- \`useChannels()\` and \`useMessages()\` → find query keys

## Problem

`sf reset` tries to stop the daemon by hitting `http://localhost:3456/api/daemon/stop` (the quarry server port), but the daemon runs on the smithy server at port 3457. This means `sf reset` silently fails to stop the daemon.

**File**: `packages/quarry/src/cli/commands/reset.ts`, line 24:
```typescript
const DEFAULT_SERVER_URL = 'http://localhost:3456';
```

**Compare with**: `packages/quarry/src/cli/commands/admin.ts`, line 491:
```typescript
const DEFAULT_SMITHY_URL = 'http://localhost:3457';
```

And `packages/quarry/src/cli/commands/serve.ts`, line 98 (smithy default port):
```typescript
const port = options.port ? parseInt(String(options.port), 10) : 3457;
```

In `reset.ts`, change `DEFAULT_SERVER_URL` to use port 3457 (the smithy server port where the daemon API lives). Consider also trying both ports (3456 and 3457) since the daemon stop endpoint could theoretically be on either server, or unify the port constants into a shared config.

Check `admin.ts` for how it handles the smithy URL — it uses `DEFAULT_SMITHY_URL = 'http://localhost:3457'` which is correct.

## Problem

TypeScript compilation in `packages/quarry` produces 3 errors (2 files) due to branded type incompatibility with `ElementId`. The root cause: `ElementId` is branded using `unique symbol`:

```typescript
// packages/core/src/types/element.ts, lines 22-23
declare const ElementIdBrand: unique symbol;
export type ElementId = string & { readonly [ElementIdBrand]: typeof ElementIdBrand };
```

When TypeScript resolves `@stoneforge/core` from different compilation units (e.g., the local workspace source vs a dist copy), each `unique symbol` declaration produces a nominally distinct symbol, making the `ElementId` types structurally incompatible. This manifests as:

```
Property '[ElementIdBrand]' is missing in type 'String & { readonly [ElementIdBrand]: unique symbol; }'
but required in type '...'
```

### Critical Bug: Component Identity Instability

The `ContainerWidthProvider` component returned by `useContainerWidthObserver()` (line 96-103 of `useContainerBreakpoint.tsx`) is defined inside a `useCallback` with `[width]` as a dependency. This is a well-known React anti-pattern.

**The problem:** Every time `width` changes (on every resize event from ResizeObserver), `useCallback` returns a new function reference. When this is used as `<ContainerWidthProvider>` in AppShell's JSX, React's reconciler sees a different component *type* (by reference identity) and **unmounts the old tree and mounts a new one from scratch**. This means:

1. **All child component state is destroyed** on every resize (form inputs, scroll positions, expanded panels, etc.)
2. **Severe performance degradation** during continuous resize (e.g., dragging the director panel edge)
3. **Visual flickering** as the entire route tree unmounts/remounts

### Fix

Define the provider as a **stable component outside the hook** so its identity never changes:

```tsx
// Stable component defined at module level — identity never changes
function ContainerWidthProviderInner({ width, children }: { width: number; children: ReactNode }) {
  const value = useMemo(() => ({ width }), [width]);
  return (
    <ContainerWidthContext.Provider value={value}>
      {children}
    </ContainerWidthContext.Provider>
  );
}

// Hook returns width + ref (not a component)
export function useContainerWidthObserver() {
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null);
  const [width, setWidth] = useState(1024);
  // ... ResizeObserver logic stays the same ...
  return { containerRef, width };
}
```

Then in AppShell:
```tsx
const { containerRef, width: containerWidth } = useContainerWidthObserver();
// ...
<main ref={containerRef} ...>
  <ContainerWidthProviderInner width={containerWidth}>
    <Outlet />
  </ContainerWidthProviderInner>
</main>
```

Export `ContainerWidthProviderInner` (or rename it to `ContainerWidthProvider`) from the hooks index if consumers need it directly.

### Minor: Unmemoized Context Value

On line 98, `value={{ width }}` creates a new object on every render, causing all context consumers to re-render even if `width` hasn't actually changed. Wrap it with `useMemo(() => ({ width }), [width])` (as shown in the fix above).

### Minor: Redundant SSR Check

Lines 67-68 have two branches that both return 1024:
```tsx
if (typeof window === 'undefined') return 1024;
return 1024;
```
Simplify to just `return 1024`.

title: Smithy Web Responsive Strategy
content:
# Smithy Web Responsive Strategy ## Overview Smithy Web uses a **content-area-aware responsive strategy** with three tiers: 1. **Content-area width** (computed in `AppShell.tsx`) — drives **sidebar** collapse/drawer decisions and **header** mobile/desktop mode. Calculated as `viewportWidth − directorPanelWidth`, so the sidebar and header respond identically whether the director panel is open or closed. 2. **Container query breakpoints** (`@sm:`, `@md:`, `@lg:`, `@xl:`) — for CSS-level responsive rules inside the main content column (header, banners, route content). 3. **Viewport breakpoints** (`sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:`) — only for components that render outside the content column (portals, overlays, modals, director panel visibility). ## Canonical Breakpoint Values All breakpoint systems (JS, CSS tokens, container queries) are aligned with **Tailwind CSS v4 defaults**: | Name | Pixels | Rem | Tailwind Container Query | |------|--------|-----|--------------------------| | xs | 0 | 0 | — | | sm | 640 | 40 | `@sm:` | | md | 768 | 48 | `@md:` | | lg | 1024 | 64 | `@lg:` | | xl | 1280 | 80 | `@xl:` | | 2xl | 1536 | 96 | `@2xl:` | ### Where These Values Live - **JS**: `apps/smithy-web/src/hooks/useBreakpoint.ts` → `BREAKPOINTS` object - **CSS tokens**: `apps/smithy-web/src/styles/tokens.css` → `--breakpoint-*` custom properties - **Container hooks**: `apps/smithy-web/src/hooks/useContainerBreakpoint.tsx` → imports from `useBreakpoint.ts` - **@stoneforge/ui**: `packages/ui/src/hooks/useBreakpoint.ts` → already uses standard Tailwind values **All four systems must use identical values.** Any change to breakpoints must update all four locations. ## Why Content-Area Width? When the director panel is open (384px default, resizable 280–800px), the main content area is significantly narrower than the viewport. If the sidebar used viewport width for collapse decisions, it would stay expanded even when the remaining content area is too small. By computing `contentAreaWidth = viewportWidth − directorPanelWidth`, the sidebar collapses at the same effective width regardless of director panel state. **The rule:** The layout must behave identically when: - Viewport is X and director panel is CLOSED - Viewport is (X + director panel width) and director panel is OPEN In both cases, the content area has X pixels, and all responsive decisions are identical. ## Sidebar Behavior The sidebar uses **content-area width** for responsive decisions, computed in `AppShell()`: ```typescript const contentAreaWidth = viewportWidth - directorPanelWidth; const isMobile = contentAreaWidth < BREAKPOINTS.md; // < 768 const isTablet = contentAreaWidth >= BREAKPOINTS.md && contentAreaWidth < BREAKPOINTS.xl; // 768-1280 ``` The `useSidebarState()` hook provides only raw state (desktopCollapsed, mobileDrawerOpen) without viewport-based logic. | Content Area Width | Sidebar State | Description | |--------------------|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------| | < 768px | Hidden (drawer) | Mobile drawer accessible via hamburger | | 768–1279px | Collapsed (icons only, w-16) | Static icon sidebar | | >= 1280px | Toggleable (w-16 or w-60) | User can expand/collapse via toggle | These thresholds match: - `@md:` (768px) — the mobile/tablet CSS boundary - `@xl:` (1280px) — the tablet/desktop CSS boundary ### Director Panel Width Tracking The director panel's expanded width is managed inside `DirectorPanel.tsx` and synced to `AppShell` via the `onWidthChange` callback prop. This ensures the content-area calculation stays accurate during resize. ### Director Panel Visibility The director panel is hidden entirely when `viewportWidth < 768` (`viewportIsMobile`). This is a viewport-level concern — the director panel renders outside the content column. ## Container Setup There are **two nested `@container` contexts** in `AppShell.tsx`: 1. **Outer container** — the main content column `
` (wraps header, banners, and `
`). Header and banner components use this container's width. 2. **Inner container** — the `
` element. Route page content uses this container's width. The `ContainerWidthProvider` wraps route content here, making container width available via hooks. ### Container Hooks (`apps/smithy-web/src/hooks/useContainerBreakpoint.tsx`) | Hook | Description | |------|-------------| | `useContainerWidth()` | Returns container width in px | | `useContainerBreakpoint()` | Returns current breakpoint name | | `useContainerIsMobile()` | `true` when container < 768px (md) | | `useContainerIsTablet()` | `true` when container 768px–1279px (md to xl) | | `useContainerIsDesktop()` | `true` when container >= 1280px (xl) | ### Viewport Hook (`@stoneforge/ui`) | Hook | Description | |------|-------------| | `useIsMobile()` | `true` when viewport < 768px | ## CSS Token @container Queries (tokens.css) The CSS tokens use `@container` queries aligned with Tailwind 4: | Query | Matches | Used For | |-------|---------|----------| | `@container (min-width: 768px)` | `@md:` | Spacing, typography, layout (tablet) | | `@container (min-width: 1024px)` | `@lg:` | Typography (large tablet) | | `@container (min-width: 1280px)` | `@xl:` | Spacing, typography, layout (desktop), sidebar expansion | ## When to Use Which ### Content-area width (via `isMobile`/`isTablet` in AppShell): - **Sidebar** collapse/drawer mode - **Header** mobile vs desktop layout (hamburger menu, breadcrumbs, command palette, toolbar buttons) ### Container queries (`@sm:`, `@md:`, etc.) and `useContainerIsMobile()`: - Route page content (anything rendered inside `
`) - Shared components used in routes: `PageHeader`, `Pagination`, etc. - Any component that renders inside the `ContainerWidthProvider` - **AppShell header** CSS-level responsive rules (padding, visibility) - **Banners** between header and main: `RateLimitBanner` ### Viewport queries (`sm:`, `md:`, etc.) and `useIsMobile()`: - **Director panel visibility** (`viewportIsMobile` in AppShell — avoids circular dependency) - **Fixed overlays/portals**: `CommandPalette`, `QuickFileOpen`, `FileContentSearch` - **Sidebars**: `NotificationSidebar` - **Modals** (via `ResponsiveModal` or `fixed inset-0`): `EmojiPickerModal`, `DocumentPickerModal`, `TaskPickerModal`, `PresetSelectionModal` ## Preventing Accidental Migration Components that should remain viewport-based have a CSS comment near their first breakpoint usage. Components that use container queries have a comment like: ```tsx {/* container-based: responds to main content column @container width */} ... ``` If a component renders outside both `@container` contexts (e.g., in a portal or modal), keep viewport breakpoints. ## Migrated Components | Component | File | Changes | |-----------|------|---------| | `AppShell` (sidebar/header logic) | `components/layout/AppShell.tsx` | Viewport `useIsMobile`/`useIsTablet` → content-area-width-based `isMobile`/`isTablet`; director panel visibility uses `viewportIsMobile` | | `AppShell` (header CSS) | `components/layout/AppShell.tsx` | `md:` → `@md:`, `lg:` → `@lg:`, added outer `@container` | | `DirectorPanel` | `components/layout/DirectorPanel.tsx` | Added `onWidthChange` callback prop for content-area tracking | | `PageHeader` | `components/shared/PageHeader.tsx` | `sm:` → `@sm:`, `useIsMobile` → `useContainerIsMobile` | | `Pagination` | `components/shared/Pagination.tsx` | `sm:` → `@sm:` | | `RateLimitBanner` | `components/layout/RateLimitBanner.tsx` | `md:` → `@md:`, `sm:` → `@sm:` | | `DaemonToggle` | `components/layout/DaemonToggle.tsx` | `lg:` → `@lg:` | | `StopAllAgentsButton` | `components/layout/StopAllAgentsButton.tsx` | `lg:` → `@lg:` |

## Problem
When all tasks in a workflow are completed (closed), the workflow itself stays in `pending` status forever. Plans have `pollPlanAutoComplete()` in the dispatch daemon (`packages/smithy/src/services/dispatch-daemon.ts:1736`) that checks active plans and auto-completes them when all tasks are closed. Workflows have no equivalent.

The utility functions `shouldAutoStart()`, `shouldAutoComplete()`, and `computeWorkflowStatus()` exist in `packages/core/src/types/workflow-create.ts` but are never called by the daemon.

## What to Change

**1. Add `pollWorkflowAutoTransition()` to the dispatch daemon**

In `packages/smithy/src/services/dispatch-daemon.ts`, add a new polling method modeled after `pollPlanAutoComplete()` (line 1736). This method should:

1. List all non-terminal workflows (`pending` and `running` status)
2. For each workflow, get its child tasks via the parent-child dependency
3. Call `computeWorkflowStatus(workflow, tasks)` from `@stoneforge/core` — this returns the suggested next status or `undefined` if no transition is needed
4. If a transition is suggested, apply it using `updateWorkflowStatus()` from `packages/core/src/types/workflow.ts`

The existing `computeWorkflowStatus()` handles all three transitions:
- `pending → running` (when any task is in_progress) via `shouldAutoStart()`
- `running → completed` (when all tasks are closed) via `shouldAutoComplete()`
- `pending|running → failed` (when any task is tombstone) via `shouldAutoFail()`

Use `api.getTasksInWorkflow(workflowId)` to get the child tasks — check that this method exists or use the dependency graph to find parent-child children of the workflow.

**2. Add to the polling interface and main loop**

- Add `pollWorkflowAutoTransition(): Promise<PollResult>` to the `DispatchDaemon` interface (around line 393)
- Add it to the `ready()` method's poll list (around line 2005) alongside `pollPlanAutoComplete()`
- Add a config flag `workflowAutoTransitionEnabled` (default: true) similar to `workflowTaskPollEnabled`

**3. Save updated workflows to JSONL (if non-ephemeral)**

Use `api.update()` to persist the status change, which handles both SQLite and JSONL sync.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Workflows auto-transition from `pending` to `running` when a task starts
- Workflows auto-transition from `running` to `completed` when all tasks close
- Workflows auto-transition to `failed` if any task is tombstoned
- The polling loop runs alongside `pollPlanAutoComplete()`
- Add tests in `packages/smithy/src/services/dispatch-daemon.bun.test.ts`

## Docs
Before starting, run `sf document search 'workflow'` and `sf document search 'dispatch daemon'` to check for relevant docs. Update any affected documentation.

## Build Failure

The build fails with the following TypeScript error:

```
src/routes/editor/index.tsx(20,36): error TS2307: Cannot find module 'monaco-editor' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

### Issue
Line 20 in `apps/orchestrator-web/src/routes/editor/index.tsx` has:
```typescript
import type * as monacoEditor from 'monaco-editor';
```

However, `monaco-editor` is not listed in `package.json` dependencies. Only `@monaco-editor/react` is installed.

### Fix Required
Add `monaco-editor` as a dependency in `apps/orchestrator-web/package.json`:

```json
"monaco-editor": "^0.52.0"
```

Or alternatively, get the types from `@monaco-editor/react` instead:
```typescript
import type { editor } from '@monaco-editor/react';
```

The `@monaco-editor/react` package should re-export types from `monaco-editor`.

After fixing, please verify the build passes with:
```bash
cd apps/orchestrator-web && pnpm build
```

**Problem:** The 'In Progress' status text in the Tasks page list view breaks to two lines when the table column is narrow. It should always stay on a single line.

   Change:

   ```
   className={`inline-flex items-center px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium rounded-full ...`}
   ```
   To:
   ```
   className={`inline-flex items-center whitespace-nowrap px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium rounded-full ...`}
   ```

2. **Line ~58** (regular status badge):
   Same change — add `whitespace-nowrap` to the className string.

### Acceptance criteria:
- 'In Progress' (and all other multi-word statuses) always renders on a single line in the Tasks list view
- No visual regressions on other badge usages
- Update docs/ if this component's behavior is documented anywhere

```typescript
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1500));
```

agent pools should have the ability to automatically create and delete agents of pre-configured types (ephemeral worker, merge steward, etc.) to fill the pool. 

e.g. if I create an agent pool that contains both ephemeral workers and merge stewards, and set the pool size to 3, then the following should happen:

* if there are less than 3 agents in the pool, then the dispatch daemon  (or the pool daemon) should check if there is a task ready to be worked on or reviewed
* if an open slot in the pool is found and a task is ready to be acted on, the corresponding agent type should be created, then spawned to work on that task
* once the task is complete (or task review complete), the agent should be deleted, freeing up the pool slot

we should likely have a configurable priority setting per pool, e.g. a priority score for each agent type to determine which agent to create when there are multiple tasks/resources demanding attention.

make sure to update the web orchestrator agents UI appropriately and add functionality to create and manage pools, both in the UI and via the CLI


handoffHistory.message:
IMPORTANT UPDATE: Do NOT stub the registerExtension function in extensions/registry.ts. The extension registration must actually work using vanilla Monaco APIs instead of @codingame.

For **theme extensions**, implement real registration:
1. Parse VS Code theme JSON format (which has `tokenColors` array with TextMate scopes and `colors` object)
2. Convert to Monaco's `IStandaloneThemeData` format (which has `rules` array with `token`/`foreground`/`fontStyle` and `colors` object)
3. Call `monaco.editor.defineTheme(themeId, convertedThemeData)` for each contributed theme
4. Track defined themes so they can be removed on uninstall (Monaco doesn't have `undefineTheme`, so track IDs and exclude from the theme picker on uninstall)

The conversion from VS Code theme format to Monaco format:
- VS Code `tokenColors[].scope` (string or string[]) → Monaco `rules[].token`
- VS Code `tokenColors[].settings.foreground` → Monaco `rules[].foreground` (strip leading #)
- VS Code `tokenColors[].settings.fontStyle` → Monaco `rules[].fontStyle`
- VS Code `colors` object maps directly to Monaco `colors`
- Set `base` to `vs-dark` or `vs` depending on the theme type (`dark` vs `light`) from the manifest
- Set `inherit: true` so unmatched tokens fall through to the base theme

For **grammar extensions** (TextMate grammars) and **snippet extensions**: these need standalone `vscode-textmate` + `vscode-oniguruma` which is out of scope for this task. Log a warning that grammar/snippet registration is not yet supported and return `{ success: true }` with the extension tracked (so it appears in the installed list) but note that only theme contributions are active.

Keep the same function signatures and types. The `registerExtension` function should iterate `manifest.contributes.themes`, load each theme JSON from the `files` map, convert it, and define it in Monaco.

## Merge Steward Review — Changes Needed ### Overall Assessment The structural approach is solid — splitting the header into a title row and controls row resolves the original issue of the Create button getting pushed to an awkward position on small screens. The search input fluid-width approach is also good. However, there is one issue that needs to be fixed before merge. ### Required Change **Use `@sm:` container query prefix instead of `sm:` media query prefix** In the Create Task button (lines ~656-657 of the current code), the responsive classes use viewport-based `sm:` breakpoints: ```tsx Create Task ``` These should use container query `@sm:` breakpoints to match the established codebase convention: ```tsx Create Task ``` **Why this matters:** The entire app uses `@container` on the `
` element (see AppShell.tsx) and all other pages use `@sm:`, `@md:`, etc. container query prefixes. When the director panel is open on a 1024px viewport, the content area is only ~600px. With `sm:` (viewport-based), the button text shows because the viewport is > 640px. With `@sm:` (container-based), it correctly hides because the container is < 640px. This directly relates to acceptance criterion #1: "The header looks clean on screens as narrow as ~600px content width." You can see the convention used in other page headers: - `apps/orchestrator-web/src/routes/merge-requests/index.tsx` — uses `@md:w-64` for search - `apps/orchestrator-web/src/routes/agents/index.tsx` — uses `@md:w-64` for search - `apps/orchestrator-web/src/routes/activity/index.tsx` — uses `@sm:flex-row @sm:items-center` ### What's Good - The two-row layout approach (title+button / controls) is clean and solves the original problem well - `min-w-0` and `shrink-0` usage for proper flex overflow handling - Search input using `flex-1 min-w-[12rem] max-w-xs` is a good responsive approach - The `truncate` on the subtitle paragraph is a nice touch ### Conflict Resolution Note I resolved merge conflicts in `apps/orchestrator-web/src/routes/tasks/index.tsx`. The branch's structural changes (two-row layout, Create button in title row) were kept. Master's inline Create button in the controls row was correctly removed since the branch intentionally relocated it. The search input's `w-full` approach was kept over master's `w-48 @md:w-64` since the branch uses a flex container wrapper.

### Issue: Use TanStack Router `<Link>` instead of plain `<a>` tag

**File:** `apps/smithy-web/src/components/agent/CreateAgentDialog.tsx` (lines 574-581 in the diff)

The "Create Workflow Template" link in the empty state uses a plain `<a href="/workflows?action=create">` tag:

```tsx
<a
  href="/workflows?action=create"
  className="..."
  data-testid="create-workflow-template-link"
>
```

This should use TanStack Router's `<Link>` component for proper client-side navigation:

```tsx
import { Link } from '@tanstack/react-router';
// ...
<Link
  to="/workflows"
  search={{ action: 'create' }}
  className="..."
  data-testid="create-workflow-template-link"
>
```

## Review Summary

Good work on tone, AI slop removal, and the URL fix. The prose sections read well and the bolding/em-dash cleanup is solid. However, the feature comparison table in the frontmatter has factual inaccuracies about OpenCode that need to be fixed before merge.

## Required Changes

### 1. Feature comparison: "One session, one task at a time" is inaccurate

OpenCode supports multi-session parallel work. Its docs describe multi-agent teams with agent coordination, and it has a subagent/task system for delegating work. The value Stoneforge adds is not "parallelism" per se (OpenCode can do that), but **orchestrated lifecycle management** — automated dispatch from a backlog, git worktree isolation per task, dependency sequencing, and merge coordination.

Suggested fix for this feature row:
- feature: "Multi-session support within a single project"
  stoneforgeAdds: "Orchestrated dispatch from a task backlog with lifecycle management"

### 2. Feature comparison: "No session recovery on failure" is inaccurate

OpenCode has built-in session recovery (auto_resume setting, error detection for tool_result_missing, etc.). What Stoneforge adds is cross-session handoff — when a session exhausts its context window or hits an unrecoverable state, Stoneforge creates a fresh session with a structured handoff containing the previous session's progress. This is different from OpenCode's within-session recovery.

Suggested fix:
- feature: "Within-session error recovery"
  stoneforgeAdds: "Cross-session handoff when context fills up or sessions fail unrecoverably"

### 3. Feature comparison: "Built-in agents within a single session" is misleading

The "within a single session" qualifier understates OpenCode. OpenCode has multi-agent teams that coordinate across sessions via message passing. Stoneforge's distinction is role-based orchestration (director/worker/steward pattern) managing independent tasks, not just "cross-instance coordination."

Suggested fix:
- feature: "Multi-agent teams with subagent delegation"
  stoneforgeAdds: "Role-based orchestration (director, worker, steward) across independent tasks"

### 4. Verify with web search

The task acceptance criteria require using WebSearch to verify every factual claim. Please verify the updated feature descriptions against OpenCode's current documentation at https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/ and https://opencode.ai/docs/ before resubmitting.

## Review Summary

The blog post is well-written with good structure, appropriate tone (humble, no AI slop), and solid SEO coverage. The build passes. However, the step-by-step tutorial section contains CLI commands that don't match the actual Stoneforge CLI, violating the task's "Accuracy" requirement: "Verify technical claims about Stoneforge match the actual codebase."

## Issues to Fix

### 1. `npm install -g @stoneforge/cli` doesn't exist
Stoneforge uses `bun` and `pnpm`, not npm. There is no published `@stoneforge/cli` npm package. Update the install step to reflect the actual installation method (clone + `bun link`, or whatever the current getting-started path is). Check the CLI reference doc (el-59tr) for the correct installation instructions.

### 2. `sf daemon start --workers 3` — `--workers` flag doesn't exist
The daemon CLI command (`packages/smithy/src/cli/commands/daemon.ts`) doesn't accept a `--workers` flag. Workers are pre-registered agent entities, not spawned by count. The daemon dispatches to available registered workers. Update the tutorial to reflect the actual daemon workflow. Check `sf daemon start --help` or the daemon CLI source.

### 3. `sf task create --depends-on <id>` — flag doesn't exist
Dependencies are managed via `sf dependency add <source> <target>`, not a `--depends-on` flag on task create. Update the example to use the correct `sf dep add` command. See the CLI reference doc (el-59tr) under "Dependency Commands."

### 4. Plan activation step missing
Plans default to `draft` status, and tasks in draft plans are NOT dispatchable (the daemon won't assign them). The tutorial creates a plan and tasks but never activates the plan. Add a `sf plan activate` step or create the plan with `--status active`.

### 5. Minor: Worker log example inconsistency
The narration says "Write tests for users endpoint" was dispatched after worker-3's endpoint task completes, but the log doesn't show worker-3 completing. The text says "(still running on worker-3) completes" which is contradictory. Clarify the log sequence so worker-3's completion appears before the dependent task is dispatched.

## Review Feedback for Agent Tool Permission Model

### Overall Assessment
The implementation is well-structured, well-tested (all 1440 tests pass), and covers most requirements thoroughly. Changesets are correct. However, one acceptance criterion is not fully met.

### Unmet Acceptance Criterion: Requirement 3 — Blocking approval flow

The task requires: "The agent should block (wait) until the request is approved or denied. On approval: execute the action and continue. On denial: return a 'permission denied' message to the agent and let it adapt."

**Current behavior:** The `PermissionMonitor` (`permission-monitor.ts`) creates an approval request when a restricted tool is detected, but it does NOT block execution. The tool executes immediately regardless. The comment on line 8-14 openly acknowledges this: "agents run with SDK permission bypass, so tools execute immediately. The monitor provides visibility..."

**What's needed:** The permission monitor needs to actually intercept and block tool execution for restricted tools. The `waitForResolution()` method on `ApprovalService` already exists and works correctly, but it's never called in the monitor flow. You need to integrate with the agent provider's tool execution pipeline so that:
1. When a restricted tool is detected, execution is paused
2. An approval request is created
3. The system waits (`waitForResolution()`) for approval/denial
4. On approval: the tool executes normally
5. On denial: a "permission denied" message is returned to the agent

This likely requires changes to the spawner service or session manager to hook into the SDK's permission callback mechanism rather than just monitoring events after-the-fact.

### Minor: Documentation Directory
The "Agent Permission Model" doc (el-30kk) was created and added to the docs library, but it was NOT added to the Documentation Directory (el-30yb). Please add an entry for it under the References table.

handoffHistory.message:
## Review Feedback — Changes Needed

The post-merge verification logic in `task.ts` is well-implemented and meets all acceptance criteria. However, there are two out-of-scope changes that must be reverted before this can be merged:

### 1. Revert the `merge.ts` change (REQUIRED)

The PR changes `packages/smithy/src/git/merge.ts` line 344 from:
```
const sourceRef = sourceBranch;
```
to:
```
const sourceRef = localOnly ? sourceBranch : \`origin/\${sourceBranch}\`;
```

This **reverts a previously-merged fix** (commit `b30aebc2` — "Fix mergeBranch() alreadyMerged check to use local refs"). The original fix was correct: `mergeBranch()` performs the actual merge using the local `sourceBranch` ref (line ~421: `merge --squash ${sourceBranch}`), so the pre-check must also use the local ref to avoid a mismatch. Using `origin/${sourceBranch}` creates a regression where unpushed local commits cause a false `alreadyMerged: true`, skipping the merge entirely. The post-merge verification then catches the discrepancy, but the result is a confusing error instead of the merge actually being performed.

**Action**: Remove the `merge.ts` change entirely. Keep the file unchanged from master.

### 2. Do NOT delete the pre-existing changeset (REQUIRED)

The PR deletes `.changeset/fix-mergebranch-alreadymerged-local-ref.md`, which exists on master. If this PR is squash-merged, that changeset would be removed from master before it's consumed by a release, losing the changelog entry for the prior fix.

**Action**: Remove the deletion of this file from the PR. It should remain unchanged.

### What's good

- The post-merge verification logic in `task.ts` (lines 454-508) correctly implements all 4 acceptance criteria
- Error messages are clear and actionable for AI steward agents
- The `commitHash` case and `alreadyMerged` case are both properly handled
- Good refactoring: reuses `execVerify` for the cleanup section instead of creating redundant imports
- Changeset `add-post-merge-verification-smithy.md` is correct (single package, patch level)

### Summary

Remove the two out-of-scope changes (merge.ts revert + changeset deletion) and the PR is ready to merge. The core task.ts implementation is solid.

title: Documentation Scan: WorkflowPresetContext targetBranch (2026-04-23)
content:
# Documentation Scan: Fix WorkflowPresetContext targetBranch (2026-04-23)

Steward: d-steward-1 (el-1k0b)
Target branch: master

## Summary

One low-complexity fix applied. No high-complexity escalations for the Director.

## Context

Since the last clean scan (2026-04-22, pass 5), master received:

- `fix: allow forward slashes in baseBranch and make review branch prompt configurable` (49363cd3)
- Version Packages (fbe5f5ab)
- Windows spawn fixes: `shellQuote` extracted to `packages/smithy/src/providers/shell-quote.ts` (c8975f4c)
- smithy-next Settings + Canvas additions (bf097a5b, a3d5aede)

## Checks Performed

| Check | Scope | Result |
|-------|-------|--------|
| File path scan | 67 active reference/how-to/explanation/spec docs, backtick-quoted full workspace paths | 0 issues (tutorial placeholders excluded) |
| Internal markdown links | `](el-xxx)` references in all active reference/how-to/explanation/spec docs | 0 broken (67 docs, all el-refs resolve) |
| CLI command references | 94 unique `sf <cmd>` invocations extracted from CLI reference docs | 0 unknown commands |
| Export/import symbols | 130 documented `import { x } from '@stoneforge/*'` checked against package sources | 3 hits, all false positives (2 tutorial placeholders, 1 multi-line re-export) |
| Documentation library membership | 65 Directory-referenced doc IDs vs library contents | 0 missing |
| Interface/type definitions | 70 unique documented types cross-checked against code | 1 issue: `WorkflowPresetContext` in el-5dgh |

## Fix Applied

### `WorkflowPresetContext` was missing the new `targetBranch` field

**Doc:** Prompts System Reference (el-5dgh) — version 9 → 10
**Source:** `packages/smithy/src/prompts/index.ts:395-396`

The interface was augmented in the `fix: allow forward slashes in baseBranch`
change to let the review workflow preset render a custom target branch.
Updated the docs block to match:

```typescript
interface WorkflowPresetContext {
  preset: WorkflowPreset;
  permissionModel: AgentPermissionModel;
  autoAllowedTools?: readonly string[];
  autoAllowedSfCommands?: readonly string[];
  allowedBashCommands?: string[];
  /** The configured merge target branch (e.g. 'stoneforge/review', 'feature/my-branch'). When set, the review preset renders this branch instead of the default `stoneforge/review`. */
  targetBranch?: string | null;
}
```

## Decision

No high-complexity issues. One low-complexity fix was applied in-place.
